2027 Clinical Pharmacology Internship Overview
Envision spending your summer working with energetic colleagues and inspirational leaders, all while gaining world-class experience in one of the most dynamic organizations in the pharmaceutical industry. This is a reality for AbbVie Interns.
AbbVie’s Clinical Pharmacology (ClinPharm) organization provides critical scientific support for all phases of pharmaceutical research and development in all divisions of the business. ClinPharm leads the design, execution, and interpretation of all clinical pharmacology Phase 1 studies, and exposure-clinical response modeling and simulation to optimize dose selection and trial design. The team also integrates data from multiple sources including preclinical and clinical pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, dosing compliance/adherence, effective and toxic exposures, financial metrics, and overall cost/benefit. Another key responsibility of the team is to present the data to regulatory authorities world-wide and authors more than half of the clinical summary documents for global regulatory submissions.
Internship projects could vary and are dependent on therapeutic area needs. Current therapeutic areas supported include Immunology, Oncology, Neurology, and Specialty assets.
Key project responsibilities include:
Analysis of literature and in-house proprietary data
Dose- and Exposure- Safety & Efficacy Endpoint Analysis
Database analyses
Development of mathematical models (e.g. PK/PD, Population PK, etc.)
Conducting simulations using mathematical models
Model-Informed Drug Development (MIDD)
Clinical study design
Presentation to the broader team at the conclusion of the assignment
Publication of authorized analyses
Minimum Qualifications
Currently enrolled in university, pursuing a PharmD or PhD in Pharmacokinetics, Pharmaceutics, Pharmaceutical Sciences, Clinical Pharmacology, or other related field
Must be returning to university for at least one semester following the internship
Preferred Qualifications
Expected graduation date between December 2027 – June 2028
Experience analyzing scientific literature and data, including database and dose- or exposure-response (safety and efficacy) analyses
Familiarity with developing and running mathematical models and simulations (e.g., PK/PD, Population PK), ideally in a Model-Informed Drug Development (MIDD) context
Understanding of clinical study design

Primary Job Function:
Position is the primary contact for brand and Copay COE teams for specific therapeutic areas Gross-to-Net Copay. Provide forecasts and modeling for all required schedules (Plan/LBE/LRP). Provide ad hoc financial analysis as needed.
Core Job Responsibilities:
Responsibilities will include, but are not limited to:
Serve as Primary contact for brand team for any CoPay related questions.
Lead all aspects for CoPay planning and reporting for Skyrizi, Rinvoq, Humira, Lutikizumab for Actuals, Plan, LBE and LRP.
Prepare all required Plan/LRP/LBE book and presentation schedules.
Work closely and collaboratively with the Copay COE team, Abbvie’s third-party CoPay provider, and MABI to gain insights on key inputs to copay (Redemption volume, cost per redemption, cohorts, etc.)
Understand and discuss all related CoPay variances for LBE/Actuals and Plan/LRP cycles.
Assist with CoPay funding, tracking, and invoice processing.
Partner with Price Accounting on the preparation of month end close journal entries, balance sheet reconciliations, and balance sheet commentary.
Additional ad-hoc project work and analysis.
Supervisory/Management Responsibilities:
There are no direct reports for this position. Rather, this position manages a complex and critical process. There is a significant individual contributor aspect to this position and requires a high level of communication with other teams and functional groups.

The Drug Product Design and Development (DPDD) group within AbbVie’s Synthetic Molecule CMC organization designs and develops drug products that enable the delivery of candidate synthetic molecules across clinical development, from proof-of-concept and pivotal studies through life-cycle innovation. DPDD collaborates with cross-functional teams to establish integrated, phase-appropriate drug product development strategies; design and execute studies that deliver bioavailable, stable, and manufacturable drug products; and ensure the timely delivery of clinical supplies. The group also optimizes formulations and manufacturing processes to produce commercially viable drug products for late stage clinical studies that meet patient needs, and support the consistent manufacture of high-quality products.
AbbVie’s DPDD organization is seeking a highly motivated, talented Scientist I with experience in formulation characterization to join our team in North Chicago, IL. The successful candidate will partner with project leads and cross-functional teams to develop drug delivery and formulation strategies; design, characterize, and build understanding of formulations and processes; and advance the biopharmaceutical characterization of clinical formulations. In this role, the candidate will serve as an integral member of the drug product team and biopharmaceutics team, executing activities that support formulation design and drug product process development. The candidate is also expected to foster productive collaborations and communicate effectively with scientific teams and cross-functional stakeholders.

Plans and executes formulation feasibility, optimization, and supporting studies for project goals. Continuously seeks to improve existing formulation techniques and processes.

title: Senior Scientist I/II - Solid Sate Characterization
description:
About AbbVie
AbbVie's mission is to discover and deliver innovative medicines and solutions that solve serious health issues today and address the medical challenges of tomorrow. We strive to have a remarkable impact on people's lives across several key therapeutic areas including immunology, oncology and neuroscience - and products and services in our Allergan Aesthetics portfolio. For more information about AbbVie, please visit us at  www.abbvie.com . Follow @abbvie on  LinkedIn,   Facebook ,  Instagram ,  X  and  YouTube.
AbbVie Analytical Research & Development (Analytical R&D) is a global analytical scientific organization responsible for all CMC analytical activities related to the development of AbbVie's pharmaceutical products.  Our scope includes AbbVie's diverse pipeline of innovative small molecule medicines and spans from the selection of Discovery candidate molecules to Late Stage Clinical.  We are building a world-class team of scientists and leaders who will drive the advancement of industry-leading analytical capabilities and make meaningful contributions to advance AbbVie's pipeline of innovative medicines.  Careers in AbbVie Analytical R&D provide unique opportunities to work with global and cross-functional teams to drive exceptional science and innovative product development strategies.  We are looking for diverse candidates with strong scientific experience to join the AbbVie Analytical R&D team and can offer exciting and rewarding career opportunities for these candidates.
Position Description:
This Senior Scientist – Solid State Characterization position will be in a technical specialty group - Physical Analytical Chemistry (PAC) withing Analytical R&D.  The PAC group is a global team of experienced and innovative scientists which utilize a diverse set of physical analytical tools to advance CMC development programs by providing insights and driving the understanding of materials, processes, and products.  Additionally, the group contributes to development and justification of control strategies and authors relevant sections of regulatory submissions across all development phases.
We are looking for a subject matter expert in X-ray and electron diffraction for crystallographic and solid-form characterization of drug substances (DS) and drug products (DP), from early form discovery through regulatory filing. The role focuses on single crystal X-ray diffraction (SCXRD), Powder X-ray diffraction (PXRD), electron diffraction (3D ED/MicroED), Rietveld refinement, quantitative phase analysis (QPA), and phase-appropriate polymorph quantitation methods both in drug substance and drug products. The scientist will work closely with Molecular Profiling Drug Development, Process Chemistry, Formulation, Process Engineering, Analytical, Operations, Quality Assurance and CMC-Regulatory.
Key Responsibilities:
Support new product development with advanced methods development and validations, technical transfer packages, and generation of technical data in support regulatory requirements.
Serve as technical SME in X-ray and electron diffraction for crystallographic and solid-form characterization of DS and DP; Responsible for PXRD method development for DS and DP, validation/technical transfer packages, and generation of technical data in support regulatory requirements
Serve as the PXRD expert for supporting solid form screening, identification, crystallinity, and stability studies; perform indexing, Pawley/Le Bail fitting, Rietveld refinement, and structure determination from powder data.
Perform quantitative phase analysis: Quantify polymorphic and amorphous content in DS and DP using Rietveld, whole-pattern, and multivariate approaches, addressing low drug load, excipient interference, preferred orientation, and micro absorption.
Apply advanced diffraction such as VT/VH-XRPD, in situ, synchrotron, and PDF analysis to study phase transformations and poorly crystalline/amorphous materials.
Apply SCXRD and 3D ED/MicroED structure determination, including absolute configuration and crystal packing of APIs, salts, cocrystals, hydrates, and solvates; generate calculated powder patterns and CIF reports.
Conduct orthogonal solid-state characterization including X-ray diffraction, thermal analysis, moisture sorption, microscopy, spectroscopy as applicable for solid form, impurity and stability studies
Support solid form control strategies per ICH Q6A, author Module 3 sections and health authority responses, and ensure GMP and data integrity compliance.
Highly autonomous and productive in performing laboratory work, method development and troubleshoot; processing, interpreting, and visualizing data to facilitate project team decisions
Represent PAC on CMC teams, lead form-change investigations, mentor scientists, and implement new diffraction technologies.
Build strong relationships with peers and cross functionally with partners outside of team to enable higher performance.
Routinely demonstrate scientific initiative and creativity in research or development activities and maintain a high level of productivity in the lab.
Understand and adhere to corporate standards regarding code of conduct, safety, appropriate handling of materials, controlled drug and radioactive compounds, and GxP compliance, where applicable.
Qualifications:
Bachelors, Masters, or Ph.D. in Chemistry, Material Science, Physics, Pharmaceutical Sciences, or a related field typically with minimum 10 (BS), 8 (MS), or 0 – 2 (Ph.D.) years related industry experience.
Strong technical background in solid state characterization, excellent analytical problem-solving, communication, presentation, and cross-functional collaboration skills. Capable of independently developing and troubleshoot analytical methods.
Extensive hands-on PXRD experience, including indexing, Rietveld refinement, QPA, and polymorph and amorphous quantitation.
Track record of developing and validating PXRD methods for DS and DP in a GMP environment, with knowledge of ICH Q2(R2), Q6A, Q14, and USP .
Expertise in small molecule SCXRD structure solution and refinement, including disorder modeling and absolute structure; and knowledge of 3D ED/MicroED approaches.
Proficiency with tools such as Olex2, SHELX, CrysAlisPro, TOPAS, Diffrac Eva and DQuant, GSAS-II, HighScore, Mercury, and the CSD.
Hands-on experience with DSC, TGA, hot-stage and polarized light microscopy, DVS, and strong data analysis and interpretation skills.

Airbnb's Online Data organization runs the stores behind every booking, every message, and every payment. Storage Foundation owns the engines underneath those stores. We build and operate Airbnb's source of truth databases for the company's online OLTP traffic, and we own the control plane that provisions, upgrades, and heals them. This is engine work, not fleet administration. When our engines are slow, unavailable, or wrong, so is the product.
As Senior Engineering Manager you will lead engineers across multiple teams and you will manage managers. You will own the engine strategy, the reliability commitment that every service above you depends on, and the growth of the people who do the work. Your leverage comes from the managers and technical leads on your teams, the bar you hold in design and incident reviews, and the trust you build with the teams who stake their product on us.
The Difference You Will Make:
Set the technical direction for Airbnb's online storage engines
You will set a multi-year technical vision for the engines and the control plane beneath every transactional and key value store at Airbnb, and you will make the calls that follow from it. That includes where we invest in our own engine expertise, where we buy instead of build, how we evaluate alternative engines against real production traffic, and which capabilities have to exist before a workload can safely land on us. You will also make the cost of these systems measurable and attributable, so that investment decisions rest on evidence. You will make these calls alongside senior technical leaders across Online Data and the broader Infrastructure organization.
Make reliability the ground truth of the platform
The services built on your engines commit to availability targets that only hold if the engine underneath them is better than they are. title: Principal Product Manager - Tech, Sales and Financial Integrity
description:
Amazon has hundreds of millions of customers, sellers, and developers all over the world that rely on Amazon products and services. Selling Partner Services (SPS) is the organization that constantly makes high judgment decisions across a wide breadth of constituents. Preserving Trust in Amazon with every customer, every transaction, every second is our mission. We do this by identifying and removing bad actors from the platform, while supporting a best-in-class customer experience. We ensure that Amazon is a safe and trustworthy place to shop and an amazing place to build a successful business selling products.
One of the key functions within SPS is to keep the financial relationship between Amazon and its sellers secure, transparent, and trustworthy. To that end, we own controls, verification, and validation for the payment instruments sellers use to pay Amazon and get paid, preventing fraud, money laundering, and financial abuse before it reaches customers or Amazon.
We're looking for a Principal Product Manager – Technical to set the long-term vision and technical product strategy for these SPS seller experiences. The role covers Bank Account Verification (BAV), Credit Card Verification (CCV), and other related seller experiences at Amazon's scale. You'll handle highly ambiguous problems that span multiple organizations, balancing fraud prevention, regulatory compliance (KYC/AML), and seller friction for millions of selling partners worldwide. You'll partner with engineering and science teams to build machine learning–driven risk decisioning and automated verification systems that detect and stop bad actors in real time, while giving legitimate sellers a fast, low-friction onboarding and payments experience. Your decisions will directly affect seller trust, onboarding success, payment reliability, fraud losses, and the integrity of Amazon's stores.
Key job responsibilities
* Own the multi-year vision, strategy, and product tenets for payment instrument verification (BAV/CCV) and related seller financial experiences, working backwards from sellers
* Set the technical direction with engineering and science leaders. This covers scalable verification architectures, machine learning–driven risk decisioning that replaces manual reviews, and systems that adapt in real time to new fraud and abuse patterns
* Build the roadmap and investment case, and make the hard trade-offs between fraud prevention, seller friction, regulatory compliance, cost, and speed to launch
* Lead initiatives that span multiple organizations, with partners in payments, fraud and abuse prevention, risk, finance, legal, and compliance. Get many teams aligned on shared goals and mechanisms
* Use voice-of-seller mechanisms, data, and experiments to raise verification success rates, reduce seller contacts, and streamline onboarding, remediation, and appeals
* Write narratives (six-pagers, PR/FAQs, planning documents) that garner support from senior product and tech leaders
* Own worldwide launches, including operational readiness and compliance in each region

* Raise the bar for product management by mentoring PMs and acting as a technical product leader across SPS
A day in the life
You might start the morning with science and engineering partners looking into a spike in failed bank account verifications. Together you'd decide whether it's a new fraud pattern or friction for legitimate sellers, and how to adjust risk controls. Later you could be in a narrative review with senior leaders about a multi-year investment in the verification platform. In the afternoon you might go through seller feedback and contact trends to set priorities for the next set of experience improvements, or coach a PM on an upcoming launch.

description:

The External System Integrations team owns that launch experience, from a shipper's first technical conversation to go-live and the first weeks of live shipping.

Amazon Shipping is seeking a Senior Program Manager to own the shipper integration launch program across the United States and Europe. Hundreds of shippers launch with us each year, from enterprise retailers with complex multi-system landscapes to mid-market shippers launching through existing software partners. You will define the program, break time to first shipment into stages the team can measure and improve, drive the dependencies that hold launches back, and build the capacity and peak plans leadership commits against. You will also run the mechanisms that keep a growing team out of firefighting: launch standards, post-launch handoff, error reduction, and a working relationship with every team we depend on.

ABOUT THIS ROLE
As a Senior Technical Program Manager focused on Business Risk, you'll serve as the strategic risk advisor to one of Audible's business organizations, partnering with its senior leaders to understand and manage the risks they face across security, fraud, content piracy, data protection, brand, and operational domains. Audible's businesses depend on a broad network of external partners, vendors, platforms, and technology, and increasingly on AI-enabled operations. Each relationship and each system is a place where unauthorized access, fraud, data exposure, or operational failure can become financial loss or harm to the Audible brand.
You will own Audible's business risk program for the organization you support end to end. You'll assess its business processes, vendor and partner relationships, and technology stack; drive remediation programs to completion with Audible InfoSec, Amazon Security, and business teams; run the recurring risk review and risk acceptance process; and own risk reporting to business and Audible leadership. Rather than building new programs, you'll use Audible's and Amazon's established risk management programs and paved path solutions, including security, fraud defense, piracy prevention, and data protection, and help the business adopt them in a way that fits how it works. Your understanding of the organization's strategy and roadmap will let you position risk management as an enabler, so the business can scale, enter new markets, and launch new initiatives safely.
ABOUT YOU
You thrive at the intersection of risk advisory and business enablement. You see risk not as a blocker but as a lens that helps a business grow safely and move faster. You are comfortable starting where the problem is not yet defined: you can take an open question such as "how exposed are we, and where?", frame the program, set its goals and success metrics, and drive it to delivery with limited guidance. You build trusted relationships with senior business leaders, translate technical risk into business language, and influence teams that do not report to you, including security, engineering, legal, and external partners. You make thoughtful trade-offs between short-term needs and long-term risk reduction, and you know how and when to escalate without damaging relationships. Your security background lets you speak credibly with security teams and understand the technical detail behind a risk. You write clear, concise narratives and are comfortable presenting risk decisions to Directors and VPs. You are a simplifier: you add process only where it earns its place, and you retire it when it no longer does.

- Proactively identify emerging risks from changes in the organization's business model, vendors, technology, and use of AI, and streamline or retire risk processes that no longer add value

title: Senior Product Manager, Forecast & Supply Automation and Analytics
description:
Apple runs one of the most complex and efficient supply chains in the world. It is powered by internal systems and tools built and managed by the GSSM Solutions & Strategy team. These tools help us manage cost and supply, and they put supply chain intelligence at the center of our decisions.
We are looking for a Senior Product Manager who understands the supply chain and can build software products that automate it. You will own tools for forecast and supply automation and analysis. You will take a complex forecast or supply problem, design the right solution, and partner with engineering to ship it. You will also present the story behind it to executives.
GSSM enables the mass production of Apple's entire product line, including iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple TV, Apple Watch, and Apple Vision Pro. The applications we build are used every day by Global Supply Managers, Material Program Managers, Suppliers, and Contract Manufacturers. They manage supply, cost, and BOM across all products and regions.
In this role, you will:
Product strategy and solution design:
• Own the product vision and roadmap. Define the strategy for forecast and supply automation and analysis tools. Prioritize work based on user pain points and business impact.
• Turn ambiguous problems into products. Take a complex forecast or supply problem, determine the right solution, and design an intuitive workflow and UI.
• Automate forecast logic. Define how forecast is calculated and translated across supply chain nodes, from finished goods through modules and components to raw materials. Work with engineering to build that logic into scalable, automated tools.
• Expose the levers. Identify the levers that influence forecast output. Build them into the product so users can model changes and see downstream impact.
• Build allocation tools. Define allocation approaches that maximize usable supply, and partner with engineering to turn them into optimization logic and user workflows.
• Build supply analytics. Deliver demand vs. supply and weeks-of-stock tools that quantify how excess or short supply affects FATP, Module CTB, and their inputs.
• Put BOM intelligence to work. Use your understanding of the BOM and the technical features of components to shape data models, reporting, and segmentation in the product.
Development and delivery:
• Translate business needs into technical requirements. Convert business requirements into clear technical requirements, user stories, and workflows that data engineering and software engineering can build against.
• Partner through development. Work with data and software engineers throughout the build. Contribute to UI design and workflow decisions, and define performance expectations. Run UAT and testing with end users.
• Lead implementation and rollout. Plan and execute launch, training, and adoption of new tools and features across user groups.
• Close the feedback loop. Gather user feedback and turn it into prioritized input for engineering to shape design. Manage production support and issue triage.
• Partner closely with users. Work daily with cross-functional teams to understand on-the-ground pain points and improve tools iteratively.
• Tell the story. Present product strategy, progress, tradeoffs, and results to executive leadership.
Minimum qualifications: Bachelors degree
7+ years of experience in product management, technical program management, or internal tools development, with strong supply chain domain expertise (supply, demand, or material planning) in hardware or consumer electronics
Strong working knowledge of BOM structures and supply chain flows, and the ability to turn them into data models, calculation logic, and product requirements
Hands-on understanding of how component and raw material forecasts are derived from finished goods demand, and experience working with engineering to automate that logic across supply chain nodes
Working knowledge of SQL, Python, or similar tools
Experience turning demand vs. supply, weeks-of-stock, and FATP and Module CTB impact analyses into tools, dashboards, and automated workflows
Experience translating business requirements into technical requirements and user stories that data engineering and software engineering teams can build against
Experience partnering with engineers and designers across the development lifecycle, including UI and workflow design, performance requirements, and UAT and testing with end users
Experience leading implementation, rollout, and adoption of software products, and managing production support
Ability to take an ambiguous forecast or supply problem from concept to a shipped product with an intuitive workflow and UI
Excellent written and verbal communication, with experience presenting product strategy and results to senior leadership
Preferred qualifications: Experience building allocation optimization or other constraint-based logic into software tools
Ability to interpret technical component specifications and incorporate them into data models, reporting, and product features
Experience gathering user feedback and turning it into prioritized product improvements
Track record of shipping internal tools, dashboards, or automation that users found intuitive
Familiarity with data pipelines, APIs, and data modeling
Familiarity with AI-assisted or agentic workflows for analysis and automation
Experience working directly with supply managers, material program managers, or contract manufacturers

title: Senior Site Reliability Engineer, Infrastructure Services
description:
Do you want to help build some of the largest and most consequential enterprise and customer technology systems in the world? Join Apple’s Information Systems and Technology (IS&T) organization.
IS&T is the engine behind everything Apple does for customers and for the people who build for them. It’s Apple’s central nervous system. Supporting 2.5 billion active Apple devices, processing billions of secure transactions, and keeping the technology that defines modern life running flawlessly, IS&T makes the impossible feel effortless.”
Do you love building solutions to handle global complexity and immense scale? Imagine what you could do here.
Infrastructure Services is part of IS&T and the foundation of Apple's global network operations — managing data center equipment and systems to deliver compute, storage, and networking services for teams across Apple, including its internal developer community. From individual facilities to a worldwide network, Infrastructure Services ensures the technology underneath everything works without question.
We are seeking a Site Reliability Engineer (SRE) with deep expertise in cloud infrastructure, production Kubernetes, and platform resilience, combined with a forward-looking mindset in AI-driven automation. This is a hands-on technical leadership role for a senior engineer with extensive SRE or DevOps experience who can architect resilient distributed systems, build production-grade tooling, and influence long-term platform strategy.

Solid grounding in distributed systems, microservices architectures, networking protocols, high availability, and disaster recovery.
Proven track record in leading production incident response, conducting root-cause investigations, and driving preventative fixes.
Hands-on experience designing and operating automated CI/CD deployment pipelines using modern tooling such as GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, or ArgoCD.

Background in building Internal Developer Platforms (IDPs) and self-service cloud infrastructure.

title: Senior Software Engineer, Development Engineering Workflows, Core OS
description:

If you want to understand how Apple's operating systems get built and reimagine how that work happens, this is that opportunity.
You will own the design and delivery of agentic workflows, backend services, and a developer platform that transforms how Core OS develops software. Prior development in Unix, Linux, or macOS.

title: Senior Software Engineer, Payments
description:
What if the payment infrastructure you built tomorrow processed millions of transactions by next quarter, across every Apple Store, the App Store, and an expanding universe of fintech partners worldwide? The Payments Engineering team sits at the core of Apple's Wallet, Payments, and Commerce organization, owning the foundational rails that make every transaction possible and pioneering capabilities like Tap to Pay on iPhone that redefine what a payment terminal can be. • Proven experience building high-availability, high-throughput distributed systems that operate reliably at significant transaction volumes.
Hands-on proficiency in Java or a JVM-based language (Kotlin, Scala) with production-grade code shipped and maintained.
Deep understanding of concurrent and asynchronous processing patterns, applied to real-world backend systems.
Track record of engaging across the full software development lifecycle, including design, testing, deployment, and on-call ownership.
Demonstrated ability to communicate technical tradeoffs clearly to cross-functional partners across engineering, privacy, and security.
Preferred qualifications: Built or operated workflow orchestration pipelines (Temporal, Apache Airflow, or similar) in a production environment.
Shipped features backed by both relational and non-relational data stores, with informed choices about consistency and query performance tradeoffs.
Hands-on experience with message queue systems (Kafka, SQS, RabbitMQ) in high-throughput, event-driven architectures.
Deployed and operated services on a major cloud platform (AWS, GCP, or Azure), including infrastructure-as-code and observability tooling.
Prior work in fintech, payments, or commerce, with direct exposure to transaction integrity, reconciliation, or regulatory compliance challenges.

title: Sensor MEMS Design Manager - Custom Silicon Management
description:

title: Silicon Debug Engineer
description:
Do you have a passion for solving the hardest problems in silicon? Do you thrive at the intersection of circuit theory, device physics, and hands-on failure investigation? As part of our Silicon Debug group, you'll take complex, often elusive silicon failures and systematically uncover their root cause — from electrical characterization all the way down to physical analysis. You and your team will apply deep engineering fundamentals and cutting-edge failure analysis techniques to enable product ramp at scale. Your efforts will directly impact the quality and reliability of state-of-the-art ASICs that power experiences for millions of customers worldwide. Join us, and you'll play a central role in ensuring the silicon we build is everything it needs to be.
We have an extraordinary opportunity for Silicon Debug Engineers to investigate and root-cause failures in advanced custom digital megacells (SRAM memories, on-chip sensors, custom data paths) used in high-performance, low-power SoCs. You will bridge the gap between electrical debug and physical failure analysis, working at the frontier of silicon investigation.
Imagine yourself at the center of our SoC bring-up and product ramp effort, collaborating across circuit design, process engineering, DFT, and failure analysis teams — with a critical impact on getting functional products to millions of customers quickly.
Minimum qualifications: A minimum of a bachelor's degree in relevant field and a minimum of 10 years of relevant industry experience.
Preferred qualifications: Experience in one or more of the following areas: SRAM circuits, custom circuit design, silicon debug.
Experience in design or debug of low-voltage / low-power custom circuits.
Deep understanding of deep-submicron device physics, leakage mechanisms, and technology interactions with device behavior.
Solid understanding of device matching, device noise sources (1/f, thermal), extrinsic noise sources (supply noise, jitter), and their impact on high-precision circuits.
Familiarity with electrical failure analysis (eFA) techniques and physical failure analysis (pFA) workflows, and the ability to plan FA strategies based on electrical debug data.
Understanding of Dynamic Lock-in Thermography (DLS) and Lock-in Thermography (LIT) for localization of resistive and leakage defects, including their sensitivity limits and how thermal signatures correlate to specific circuit fault modes.
Knowledge of Nanoprobe techniques for electrical probing of deep-submicron nodes, and appreciation of how probe contact, voltage bias, and electron beam exposure can perturb sensitive analog or memory circuits.
Awareness of how physical sample preparation steps (deprocessing, FIB cross-section, delayering) can alter or destroy evidence of electrical failures, and how to coordinate FA plans that preserve failure signatures.
Ability to interpret FA results (photon emission maps, OBIRCH, thermal maps, TEM/SEM imagery) in the context of circuit topology and failure electrical signatures.
Ability to conduct structured experiments during silicon debug, gather and analyze large datasets, and utilize scripting to support efficient handling of debug data.
Proficiency in scripting languages (Python, Perl, or others) and CAD automation tools.
Knowledge of industry-standard circuit design and simulation tools.

title: Silicon Material Engineering Project Specialist
description:

Experience in data visualization and dashboard creation

title: Silicon Validation Engineering Program Manager
description:
Imagine what you could do here. At Apple, new insights have a way of becoming extraordinary products, services, and customer experiences very quickly. title: Software Engineer - Camera
description:
Apple's Camera ISP team is looking for a passionate and skilled embedded software engineer to help shape the future of imaging across all Apple products. title: Software Engineer- Spatial Media and Graphics, Vision Products Software
description:
Apple is where individual imaginations gather together, committing to the values that lead to great work. title: Software Engineering Manager - AI & Data Platforms
description:
Apple builds products and services that enrich people's lives. Athena Platform Services builds the data and machine learning platforms that power fraud, waste, and abuse prevention across Apple. We are looking for a highly technical, hands-on Software Engineering Manager to lead this work and grow a high-performing engineering team. from the front, contribute to technical direction and implementation, drive execution, and foster a culture of collaboration, ownership, accountability, and continuous improvement.

title: Growth Analytics
description:
ABOUT BASE

Base is America’s next-generation power company. We’re rebuilding the foundation of modern civilization–electricity–by deploying a vast network of distributed batteries that is transforming today’s fragile, centralized grid into a resilient and abundant system. We are engineers, operators, and creatives solving some of the most complex, interdisciplinary challenges of our time.




ABOUT THE ROLE

Base is looking for an excellent operator to help scale the systems behind our customer acquisition engine.

This role is responsible for increasing the speed, intelligence, and effectiveness of how our customer acquisition team operates. You will drive experimentation, while building the systems, automation, and infrastructure that make that experimentation scalable.

The ideal candidate is highly resourceful, systems-oriented, technically curious, and obsessed with finding leverage. You should be equally comfortable thinking strategically, digging through data, building workflows, launching experiments, and executing quickly in ambiguous environments.

 


WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Build systems, workflows, and dashboards that improve the speed and effectiveness of the customer acquisition team.

 - Drive experimentation across customer acquisition initiatives.

 - Build operational infrastructure that improves measurement, reporting, attribution, funnel visibility, and experimentation velocity.

 - Partner closely with Product, Engineering, Data, Sales, and Member Experience teams to improve systems across the funnel.
   
    


WHAT YOU'LL BRING

 - 1+ years of experience working in a fast-paced environment.

 - You are highly execution-oriented and naturally default toward building, shipping, and improving systems.

 - You’ve built workflows, operational systems, or experimentation frameworks that drove measurable business outcomes.

 - Strong systems thinking: you instinctively identify bottlenecks, friction, and opportunities for operational leverage.

 - Analytical ability and comfort working with data, funnels, attribution, experimentation, and customer behavior.

 - Ability to operate independently and execute quickly in ambiguous, fast-moving environments.

 - Strong judgment and a bias toward action.

 - High ownership and accountability.
   
    


PREFERRED SKILLS

 - Experience working large data sets in BigQuery (or similar data warehouses).

 - AI workflows, operational automation, or internal tooling that improved execution or business performance.

 - Strong analytics fluency, including SQL and product analytics platforms such as PostHog, Amplitude, or Mixpanel.

 - Experience with experimentation frameworks, funnel analysis, segmentation, and attribution systems.

 - Experience operating in high-growth startup environments.




ABOUT THE TEAM

The Growth team at Base is lean, high-ownership, and results-driven. We operate with clear accountability, tight feedback loops, and a strong bias towards action. Marketing works closely with design, sales, and product to build scalable systems that support the rapid buildout of America's next-generation power company.



Please note: Base is a startup, which means priorities shift and evolve quickly. Your role may expand or change based on the needs of the business at any given time, so the responsibilities listed may not be exhaustive.




OUR VALUES

 - First Principles Thinking: Question assumptions. Principles > rules.

 - Operate at Base Pace: Focus on what matters, act quickly, and learn by doing.

 - Give & Get Feedback: Be direct, be humble, and maintain a growth mindset.

 - Everyone’s an Owner: Follow through on commitments and own results.

 - Strong Opinions, Loosely Held: Drive clarity and make calls with imperfect information.

 - Committed to the Mission: Rebuilding the grid is a big challenge. We work hard because we care deeply about the impact we’re creating. We work in-person. It’s not a 9-to-5. We are all-in.

 - Fun & Optimism Coexist with Grit: Collaboration and celebration coincide with the intensity of building real things.
   
   


DO THE BEST WORK OF YOUR LIFE AT BASE.

The Dealer.com Performance Manager is expected to build and maintain relationships with external clients and ensure client needs are the driving force behind priorities, decisions, and activities in order to ensure success through product utilization, product upgrades, group harvest sales, and  revenue retention. The Performance Manager owns the client relationship on behalf of the company and will act as the client advocate internally by communicating the client’s needs to various departments.
The Performance Manager works remotely under limited supervision and responsible for protecting monthly revenue where no long term client contracts may be in place.  The Performance Manager is also responsible for identifying the level of customer interest in additional products, harvesting additional accounts, and expanding/upselling product functionality to potentially increase revenue growth across their client base.  The Performance Manager is expected to collaborate with other Performance Managers to ensure clients with multiple products encounter a seamless and consistent experience.
What You'll Do
Responsible for external client and revenue retention by working independently to effectively managing the progress and results of all accounts assigned within their portfolio.
Build upgrade/harvest revenue opportunities and maintain relationships with a portfolio of clients to ensure client goals are the driving force behind priorities, decisions, and activities with a portfolio of clients and ensure customers’ needs are the driving force behind every priority, decision, and activity. Will carry a full and/or complex account load.
Retain clients by engaging with each client through virtual screen share engagements and occasional onsite visits that increase product utilization, improved processes and client goal attainment to drive valuable insights to increase product utilization and improving client’s business processes and helps them meet their objectives.
Build and develop strong working relationships with clients and all client staff at all levels from within the dealership.
Works with ‘at risk’ clients, using Consultative strategies to identify and develop an action plan to turn around and retain the relationship.

Demonstrate responsiveness to client contact and provide guidance they need, not just what they ask for. Proven ability to influence clients on how to use and leverage the capabilities of the product to meet their business objectives.
Monitor and analyze account performance and trends to determine adjustments to dealer expectations/goals/objectives in order to achieve results.
Closely monitor system ‘red flags’/emergencies with clients and take immediate action.
Improve existing processes & systems using conceptualizing, reasoning & interpretation during engagement with clients.
Responsible for maintaining product knowledge and trainings, including new releases and enhancements to products in their direct AOR.
Works Independently to identify and moderate complex issues.

4+ years experience in a retail automotive dealership setting
4+ years managing digital marketing strategies for a single rooftop or dealer group
Proven sales acumen

Demonstrates openness to change and actively embraces new technologies to enhance operational efficiency.

Track progress to help clients reach performance goals using software and collaboration with software partners

description:

Compensation
Compensation includes a base salary in the range of $148,500.00 - $247,500.00. The base salary may vary within the anticipated base pay range based on factors such as the ultimate location of the position and the selected candidate’s knowledge, skills, and abilities. Position may be eligible for additional compensation that may include an incentive program.
Job Description
The Director of Operations & Risk Management is a senior leader who owns dealer and inventory operations for the Autotrader Consumer Marketplace. The Director champions the dealer perspective throughout strategy development and execution, ensuring that dealer impact, feasibility, and risk are weighed in the decisions that shape the marketplace. This leader also owns the commercial relationships, partner economics, and contracts for the vendor relationships required to enable Consumer Marketplace success.
The Director builds a repeatable system for turning dealer needs, feedback, and root causes into global standards, audits, and policy . This leader translates dealer group client needs into product and commercialization requirements, shapes market and sales positioning, and carries thought leadership with dealers and partners. The Director brings dealer and risk insight to marketplace health strategy and day-to-day execution, working closely with the Business Readiness and Strategic Planning leaders.
The Director protects the marketplace by working with boundary partners to own billing, legal, regulatory, compliance, consent, pricing transparency, and brand risk for the business. This includes leading the Consumer brand management and fraud team. This role requires close partnership with Legal, Compliance, Sales, Product, and Client Services, and serves as a trusted advisor to executives on dealer sentiment, risk, and commercial exposure.
*Atlanta is the preferred location but can be remote anywhere in the USA.*
Primary Duties and Responsibilities:
Dealer Escalation & Marketplace Operations
Own key client escalation and mitigation across all segments, with primary ownership for dealer and public groups and their vendors.
Convert escalation root causes into global standards and audits , turning firefighting into policy.
Oversee dealer and inventory operations, including accounts, listings, and billing and invoicing optimization and management .
Own market and sales positioning, including Voice of Field and nVision access and user agreements.
Dealer Relationships & Commercial Strategy
Own senior relationships with dealer and public group leadership and their vendors.
Lead vendor and partner economics and negotiation for dealer clients (e.g., Experian), with strong fluency in vendor contract and payment/breach terms and the ability to build strategic options.
Coordinate vendor work with Legal on terms, exposure, and exit paths.
Translate dealer group client needs into product and commercialization requirements.
Coordinate RFI responses with solution design, applicable SMEs, and account teams.
Lead vendor and partnership development, including thought leadership that positions Autotrader with dealers and partners.
Risk, Legal, Regulatory & Brand
Own legal, regulatory, consent, pricing transparency, and compliance management, partnering with Legal and Compliance.
Own brand, regulatory, and enterprise risk management , and lead the Consumer brand management and fraud team.
Embed compliance and risk requirements into launches and marketplace changes in partnership with Business Readiness.
Dealer Voice in Strategy & Execution
Champion the dealer perspective throughout strategy development and execution, bringing dealer impact, feasibility, and risk into portfolio, product, and growth decisions.
Maintain competitive intelligence with field and dealer input and share it with Strategic Planning and Product.
Contribute dealer insight to marketplace health strategy and day-to-day marketplace execution, working with the Business Readiness & Execution and Strategic Planning leaders.
Cross-Functional Influence & Executive Partnership
Serve as a trusted advisor to executives, offering data-driven insights on dealer sentiment, risk, and commercial exposure that balance speed, quality, and adoption.
Represent dealer, operations, and risk perspectives in cross-enterprise forums, shaping portfolio priorities, funding, and resourcing decisions.
Partner with boundary organizations (Product, Engineering, Sales, Marketing, Client Services, Legal) to resolve dealer issues and align on standards and policy.
Represent Autotrader and Consumer Marketplace capabilities as a thought leader to dealer groups, industry partners, and automotive media.
Capability Building & Team Leadership
Build and mentor a high-performing team that blends dealer operations, risk management, process optimization, and data literacy.
Establish success metrics for escalation resolution, repeat-issue reduction, and dealer satisfaction.
Foster a culture of continuous learning through retrospectives, performance insights, and knowledge-sharing across teams.
Financial & Vendor Management
Monitor budgets to ensure adherence to cost and performance targets.
Manage vendor relationships and external partnerships that support dealer operations and risk management.
Required Experience & Specialized Knowledge and Skills:
BS/BA degree in related discipline required with 10+ years of experience in related field with at least 5 years’ experience in a leadership role OR 14 years of experience with no degree.
10+ years of experience in related field with at least 5 years’ experience in a leadership role
3-5-year track record of creating and implementing strong processes and standards that have demonstrated a positive influence on client satisfaction and employee productivity
Demonstrated experience managing dealer or enterprise client escalations and senior-level commercial relationships at large dealer groups or comparable clients
Working knowledge of legal, regulatory, and compliance requirements affecting digital marketplaces or automotive retail, including consumer protection and pricing transparency
Demonstrated leadership, initiative and follow through required
Strong cross-functional collaborator with proven ability to communicate effectively at all levels of the organization
Experience negotiating and managing vendor and partner contracts, including economics, terms, and exit paths
Generates innovative ideas and solutions to challenges/opportunities
Strong analytical skills and demonstrated experience translating dealer and client needs into clear product, policy, and operational requirements
Self-starter with ability to work with minimal supervision
Demonstrated client obsession and excellent expectation-management abilities
Must be able to influence and coach individuals across the organization
Effective at working in a highly matrixed environment
Extensive professional knowledge of the automotive retail, dealer, and marketplace industry and regulatory trends preferred

Job Description
****EOE, including disability/vets****
Cox Fleet Academy is a paid training program designed to prepare you for a full-time career as a Diesel Mechanic with Cox Fleet . We provide the training, tools, mentorship, and hands-on experience you need to build your career.
Cox Fleet is one of the largest fleet maintenance companies in the country, providing mobile maintenance and repair services for light, medium, and heavy-duty trucks and trailers nationwide.
If you enjoy working with your hands, solving mechanical problems, and want a long-term career with room to grow, this could be the opportunity for you.
What You’ll Get
As a Cox Fleet Academy Diesel Mechanic, you will receive:
Paid technical training at our Academy in Indianapolis, IN
Company-paid travel and hotel accommodations while attending the Academy
A meal stipend during qualifying classroom training
A set of hand tools and toolbox provided to you
Hands-on mentorship with an experienced Cox Fleet Technician
A defined training and pay progression
The opportunity to transition into a full-time Diesel Mechanic position
Continued technical development as you progress through the program
Diesel Academy Training & Pay Progression:
First Academy Training:
5 weeks of paid classroom and technical training in Indianapolis, IN
$16.00/hour or applicable state minimum wage, whichever is greater
$250 per week (taxable) stipend for the first week only.
Field Mentorship:
Approximately 8 to 10 weeks of hands-on mentorship in your home market
$19.00/hour
Second Academy Training:
Return to Indianapolis for an additional 5 weeks of paid technical training
$19.00/hour
$250 per week (taxable) stipend for five weeks.
Upon Graduation:
$21.00/hour
What You’ll Learn
Your training will help build the foundation needed to maintain and repair fleet vehicles, including:
Diesel engine fundamentals
Preventive maintenance
Vehicle inspections
Basic diagnostic and troubleshooting skills
Brake and suspension systems
Electrical fundamentals
General truck maintenance and repair
Proper use of tools and shop equipment
Safety procedures and industry best practices
Following classroom training, you will continue developing your skills alongside an experienced technician in the field.
What We’re Looking For
We are looking for candidates who bring:
A genuine desire to build a career as a Diesel Mechanic
Mechanical aptitude and an interest in repairing vehicles or equipment
Willingness and ability to successfully complete an intensive technical training program
Ability to travel to Indianapolis for required Academy training
Ability to operate an iPad and learn digital work-order systems
High school diploma or equivalent combination of education preferred, but not required
Valid state-of-residence driver's license
Ability to obtain and maintain a Driver Qualification File
Ability to meet applicable DOT and FMCSA requirements

Road test vehicles to identify issues, verify repairs and ensure they are operating safely and properly.

title: Machine Builder
description:
Who we are:
Formic is on a mission to reshape American manufacturing by making automation accessible to every factory. As labor constraints rise, costs increase, and global competition intensifies, automation is no longer optional for manufacturers that want to stay competitive.
We deliver automation through a Robotics-as-a-Service model that combines industrial robotics, proprietary software, and full-service support into a single, integrated solution. By removing the traditional barriers of cost, complexity, and risk, we enable manufacturers to deploy automation quickly and realize measurable gains in throughput, safety, and operational efficiency without large upfront capital investment.
Backed by leading investors including Lux Capital, Initialized Capital, Blackhorn Ventures, and Mitsubishi HC Capital North America, Formic is scaling rapidly and building the foundation for a new era of high-performance, Made in America production.
About the team:
The Automation Engineering Team is responsible for delivering robotics-driven automation deployments across a wide range of customer applications. The team partners cross-functionally to translate customer requirements into deployed systems, ensuring solutions are integrated, commissioned, and validated to perform reliably in real manufacturing environments. Automation Engineering works closely with customers, internal technical teams, and external integrators to execute deployments on schedule while maintaining high standards for quality, safety, and repeatability.
About the role:
As a Machine Builder, you will play a critical role in bringing Formic’s robotic systems into live production environments. You will support system integration through hands-on build, configuration, testing, troubleshooting, and validation in the shop, followed by on-site installation and commissioning at customer facilities.
In this role, you will:
Support internal system integration for robotics-driven automation solutions, including mechanical and electrical setup, quality checks, documentation, testing, program updates, troubleshooting, FAT, and final pack-out
Install and commission Formic solutions at customer sites in close collaboration with Deployment Engineers and Project Managers
Perform mechanical installation, power-up, testing, troubleshooting, fine-tuning, performance validation, and final documentation
Support refurbishment and reconditioning of returned systems as needed
Validate system performance and identify improvements during testing, commissioning, and live production deployments
Test and troubleshoot new automation solutions under development
Follow Formic’s standardized processes, tools, SOPs, and all applicable safety requirements
Coordinate with OEMs, vendors, and system integration partners to support system delivery, quality, and continuous improvement initiatives
Support early-stage product deployments, including hands-on installation, commissioning, and validation of newly developed automation solutions
Provide diagnostics and troubleshooting support for newly deployed products that have not yet transitioned to the service team
Document lessons learned and help develop SOPs, deployment procedures, and best practices to support scalable product rollouts
What makes you a great fit:
Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Mechatronics, or a related field, or equivalent hands-on experience
3+ years of hands-on experience with industrial 6-axis robots in installation, maintenance, repair, programming, troubleshooting, or technical support roles
3+ years of experience installing and commissioning industrial machinery
Experience with end-of-line automation systems such as robotic palletizing, depalletizing, and case packing preferred
Willingness to travel up to 50–60% for multi-day customer deployments and commissioning activities
Highly action-oriented with strong problem-solving instincts and the ability to navigate unfamiliar challenges independently
Clear, confident written and verbal communication skills
Comfortable using hand tools and working in hands-on technical environments
Strong PC and general technical proficiency
Valid driver’s license and access to a personal vehicle for local travel (mileage reimbursed per Formic policy)
Ability to lift 50+ pounds
Ability to work independently while representing Formic professionally in customer environments
Experience with industrial robots such as FANUC, ABB, KUKA, Yaskawa/Motoman, or Universal Robots preferred
Our Total Rewards:
At Formic, we believe people do their best work when they feel supported both professionally and personally. That’s why we offer a comprehensive benefits and perks package for full-time, U.S.-based team members, including:
Equity in Formic: Participate in our stock option program and share in the success of a fast-growing start-up backed by leading global investors
Competitive & Uncapped Commission Structure: Designed to reward performance and impact in commission-eligible roles
Comprehensive Healthcare Coverage: Medical, dental, and vision insurance through Blue Cross Blue Shield and Unum, with 99% of employee premiums covered and 75% coverage for dependents, with optional buy-up plans available
Additional Insurance Benefits: FSA and DCFSA, life insurance, short-term disability, and long-term disability through Unum, all 100% employer-paid
Employee Assistance Program (EAP): Fully funded by Formic, offering support when you need it most
Paid Parental Leave Program: Up to 12 weeks of paid parental leave
Company-sponsored 401(k): Invest in your future with our company-facilitated retirement savings plan
Home Office Stipend: A one-time allowance for fully remote and hybrid employees to support an at-home or on-the-road work setup
Monthly Cell Phone Reimbursement: Monthly stipend toward personal phone and internet expenses
Flexible Time Off: Take the time you need, when you need it, supported by our flexible PTO policy
Compensation Philosophy
Formic’s pay and equity packages are thoughtfully benchmarked against peer companies at a similar growth stage. Equity represents a meaningful part of our mutual investment: when Formic succeeds, so do you.
Final offers are customized based on experience, geographic location, market considerations, and a candidate’s preferred balance of cash and equity. Our goal is to attract and reward top talent who will have significant impact, and we are open to thoughtful discussions to align on the right structure.
Compensation Range: $28 — $38 USD What we look for:
We’re building this company from the ground up, and every person we hire has an outsized impact on our culture, performance, and trajectory. While each team member brings unique strengths and perspectives, we look for people who align with our Operating Principles and embody them in action. If this sounds like you, Formic may be the right place for you!
Fearless Optimism: You make bold bets and default optimistic. You believe in the mission, aren’t paralyzed by risk, and fear inaction more than failure. You see ambiguity as opportunity and bring energy to building what doesn’t yet exist.

POSITION SUMMARY
The Demand Planner is responsible for developing and maintaining accurate demand forecasts to support business objectives, customer service, and effective supply chain planning. This role partners cross-functionally with Sales, Finance, Operations, and other key stakeholders to understand demand drivers, improve forecast performance, and support the Sales & Operations Planning (S&OP) process. The Demand Planner leverages data analytics, forecasting tools, and continuous improvement practices to strengthen planning effectiveness and support informed business decisions.
Location: Hybrid – Deerfield, IL. In office Tuesday–Thursday, with the option to work remotely Monday and Friday.
KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
Develop, maintain, and analyze demand forecasts using historical trends, statistical forecasting methods, market intelligence, and business inputs.
Collaborate with Sales, Finance, and other cross-functional partners to understand demand drivers, identify risks and opportunities, and develop a consensus demand plan.
Support the monthly Sales & Operations Planning (S&OP) process through demand analysis, forecast reviews, and communication of key assumptions and changes.
Monitor forecast accuracy and bias, identify root causes of variances, and implement improvements to forecast performance.
Incorporate relevant business factors, including seasonality, promotions, customer trends, and product lifecycle changes, into demand planning.
Partner with Supply Planning and Operations to align demand forecasts with supply and inventory planning requirements.
Apply forecasting tools, advanced analytics, and generative AI modeling to develop new forecasts, refine existing forecasts, and improve planning effectiveness.
Support annual business planning and other financial planning activities by providing demand projections and relevant analysis.
Identify and implement opportunities for process standardization, automation, and continuous improvement within demand planning.
REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS
Bachelor's degree in Supply Chain Management, Business, Finance, Analytics, or a related field preferred; equivalent relevant experience considered.
Minimum of 2 years of experience in demand planning, forecasting, supply chain planning, or related analytical roles.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to interpret data and translate findings into actionable insights.
Advanced Microsoft Excel skills and proficiency working with large data sets.
Familiarity with demand planning methodologies, forecasting techniques, and key performance indicators.
Strong communication, collaboration, and presentation skills, with the ability to work effectively across functions.
Ability to manage multiple priorities, demonstrate initiative, and adapt to changing business requirements.
Proficiency with business systems and analytical tools; experience with, or willingness to learn, generative AI applications for forecasting and analysis.
PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS
Experience in manufacturing, distribution, retail, or other complex supply chain environments.
Familiarity with Sales & Operations Planning (S&OP) or Integrated Business Planning (IBP) processes.
Experience with ERP systems, demand planning software, or business intelligence tools.
Experience with statistical forecasting, advanced analytics, or automation tools.
APICS CPIM/CSCP or Institute of Business Forecasting (IBF) certification.

title: Product Commercialization Engineer
description:
Job Description:
SUMMARY:
The Product Commercialization Engineer will get to work in a fast-paced and dynamic environment, leading the scale-up and commercialization of adhesive, coating, and polymer technologies from laboratory development to full-scale manufacturing. This hands-on role partners with R&D, Operations, Engineering, Quality, EHS, Procurement, and Supply Chain to solve scale-up challenges and ensure products are manufactured safely, reliably, and cost-effectively across epoxy, acrylic/methacrylate, polyurethane, and hybrid polymer systems. This is an exciting opportunity to be part of driving innovation and growth for a division within a market-leading, Fortune 200 organization!
ITW BUSINESS MODEL & CULTURE
We have an environment shaped by our decentralized, entrepreneurial culture that brings our exciting ideas to life.  Our people thrive in our “flexibility within the framework” approach.
We are committed to providing you with growth and development opportunities that maximize your unique potential.
Our culture empowers you to think and act like a business owner – we want your entrepreneurial spirit to thrive!
Be a part of One ITW/One Team, where everyone’s contribution matters in our quest to achieve our full potential.
We live by our Core Values: simplicity, sharing risk, integrity, respect, and trust.
YOU MIGHT LIKE THIS JOB IF YOU ARE...
Are an entrepreneurial self-starter. You take initiative and ownership of your surroundings and constantly seek to find ways to improve.
Thrive in a fast-paced environment that keeps you on your toes – you love a good challenge, meeting aggressive deadlines, and can stay calm under pressure.
Have a passion for innovation and creating new technologies to solve customer pain points and market applicability.
Are resilient. You enjoy finding solutions to complex challenges and do so with poise and resolve.
Can work well with cross functional teams and lead by example. You have strong communication skills and the ability to influence without authority.
PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIES:
Product Commercialization & Scale-Up
Lead commercialization and scale-up of new adhesive, coating, and polymer products from lab to full-scale manufacturing.
Develop robust, reproducible, and scalable manufacturing processes using chemical engineering principles and process science.
Identify and mitigate scale-up risks related to mixing, reaction control, heat transfer, equipment capability, and process variability.
Define operating windows and critical process parameters to ensure quality, consistency, and manufacturability.
Manufacturing & Process Improvement
Serve as a technical expert in polymer chemistry, process control, mixing, manufacturability, and raw material interactions.
Drive process improvements that enhance safety, quality, throughput, cost efficiency, and waste reduction while maintaining product performance.
Lead manufacturing troubleshooting, root-cause investigations, and resolution of batch variability and scale-dependent performance issues.
Apply DOE, statistical analysis, and structured problem-solving tools to optimize processes and resolve manufacturing challenges.
Change Management & Process Technology
Lead evaluation, validation, and implementation of raw material, process, equipment, and manufacturing site changes, including alternative and second-source materials.
Identify, evaluate, and implement new manufacturing technologies, process controls, equipment, and analytical tools that support commercialization and operational excellence.
Support equipment qualification, process commissioning, manufacturing start-ups, and production readiness activities.
Safety, Quality & Leadership
Provide technical leadership across R&D, Operations, Quality, EHS, Supply Chain, suppliers, and external partners to deliver safe, compliant, cost-effective, and successful product commercialization.
Promote, support, and adhere to all safety, environmental and quality related policies and procedures .
QUALIFICATIONS, SKILLS, & COMPETENCIES:
B.S. in Chemical Engineering or a closely related engineering discipline.
Minimum 5 years of experience in product/process scale-up and commercialization within a chemical manufacturing environment, including transfer from laboratory through pilot to commercial production.
Demonstrated experience bridging R&D/product development and manufacturing operations, including technology transfer and support of production scale-up between sites. Demonstrated track record of successfully commercializing new products at industrial production scale.
Strong knowledge of chemical engineering fundamentals, including mixing, heat transfer, mass transfer, reaction engineering, process control, and industrial manufacturing equipment/processes.
Proven ability to troubleshoot manufacturing and product-quality issues using structured problem-solving methods, including DOE, statistical analysis, process data analysis, and root-cause investigation; proficiency with tools such as JMP or Minitab preferred.
Demonstrated experience qualifying raw materials and alternate sources in incumbent commercial products.
Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to collaborate effectively across technical, operational, and manufacturing teams.
Experience preferred in the adhesives, coatings, sealants, specialty polymers, or formulated chemical products industries, primarily with epoxy, polyurethane, acrylic/methacrylate, and/or hybrid polymer chemistries.
Travel:  Ability to travel periodically to manufacturing facilities, suppliers, and partner locations within the United States. Occasional international travel may be required.

The salary for this role is $100,000.00 - $125,000.00. This is the range that we in good faith anticipate relying on when setting wages for this position. We may ultimately pay more or less than the posted range and this range. This salary range may also be modified in the future.

title: Sr Buyer - Precision Welding Solutions Divison
description:
Job Description:
The Senior Buyer is a key supply chain leader responsible for driving procurement, supplier performance, inventory management, and continuous improvement initiatives within the Precision Welding Solutions Division. In this role you will partner closely with the Materials Manager, suppliers, engineering and cross-functional teams to ensure excellence in cost, quality and delivery.
You will provide leadership, develop talent and drive results across the Precision Welding Solutions Division.  The ideal candidate thrives in a fast-paced environment, demonstrates strong negotiation and relationship building skills and can drive change through collaboration and influence.
How You Will Make an Impact:
Supply Chain & Procurement
Manage procurement activities, including sourcing, purchasing, inventory planning, and material flow.
Lead supplier negotiations involving pricing, contracts, delivery performance, and service levels.
Evaluate, select, and develop suppliers in partnership with the Materials Manager and engineering team.
Build collaborative supplier relationships while identifying opportunities for supplier consolidation and risk reduction.
Conduct supplier visits, audits, and performance reviews.
Manage supplier corrective action processes and ensure timely resolution of quality or delivery issues.
Monitor and communicate Market Rate of Demand (MRD) changes to suppliers
Cost & Inventory Management
Drive cost reduction, productivity, quality, delivery, and simplification initiatives.
Manage material price variance, inventory turns, and inventory optimization programs.
Track and document cost savings and cost avoidance projects.
Maintain inventory accuracy through cycle count oversight and inventory management practices.
Support inventory transition activities related to product launches, engineering changes, and product obsolescence.
Manage MOH and inactive inventory performance metrics.
Strategic Initiatives
Lead or support divisional materials and supply chain improvement projects.
Develop and implement materials strategies aligned with business objectives.
Actively participate in New Product Development (NPD) initiatives.
Partner daily with manufacturing, engineering, and other cross-functional teams to ensure material availability and operational continuity.
Champion and implement ITW business principles, including 80/20, Product Line Simplification, Market Rate of Demand (MRD), Empowerment, Trust, and Continuous Improvement.
Leadership & Talent Development
Provide leadership, coaching, and support to materials personnel and cross-functional teams.
Depending on organizational needs and candidate experience, the role may include direct supervision of materials personnel.
Identify opportunities to simplify processes, improve efficiency, and develop organizational capabilities
How You Show Up:
Collaborative Leader – Builds strong relationships through effective leadership, communication and interpersonal skills.
Supplier Partnership – Builds and maintains supplier relationships while driving negotiation, quality, delivery and cost performance.
Ownership Mindset – Takes initiative to lead cost reduction, inventory management and new product development projects.
Results-Driven – Prioritizes effectively, approaches challenges analytically and follows through to achieve results.
Growth Mindset – Demonstrates a commitment to continuous learning, professional development and personal growth.
Qualifications:
Bachelor’s Degree in Supply Chain Management, Operations, Business Management or related field.
3 years of experience in purchasing, sourcing, supply chain or materials management.
Experience coaching, developing or leading teams either through direct supervision or cross-functional leadership
Proficiency with Microsoft office applications
Company Description
Comprised of a market-leading portfolio of best-in-class brands, the businesses of ITW Welding work together to provide premium performance delivered through a breadth of solutions encompassing welding, cutting, consumables, and accessories.  ITW Welding North America represents Miller Electric Welding Equipment, Safety & Accessories, Hobart Filler Metals, and Bernard / Tregaskiss MIG Guns.
Miller Electric Mfg. LLC, is headquartered in Appleton, Wisconsin, and wholly owned by  Illinois Tool Works  (NYSE: ITW). The company maintains its industry leadership by setting the standard for reliability, quality and responsiveness. Our tagline, “The Power of Blue®,” is inspired by the blue color of Miller equipment.
The company began with an innovation that responded to customer needs, growing from a one-man operation in 1929, to the world’s largest manufacturer of arc welding products. Miller keeps the tradition alive by focusing on its top priority: people.
