title: Analyst, EFT Trade Compliance and Operations (Bi-Lingual English/Spanish)
description:
It started with a simple idea: what if surgery could be less invasive and recovery less painful? Nearly 30 years later, that question still fuels everything we do at Intuitive . As a global leader in robotic-assisted surgery and minimally invasive care , our technologies—like the da Vinci surgical system and Ion —have transformed how care is delivered for millions of patients worldwide.
We’re a team of engineers, clinicians, and innovators united by one purpose: to make surgery smarter, safer, and more human. Every day, our work helps care teams perform with greater precision and patients recover faster, improving outcomes around the world.
The problems we solve demand creativity, rigor, and collaboration. The work is challenging, but deeply meaningful—because every improvement we make has the potential to change a life.
If you’re ready to contribute to something bigger than yourself and help transform the future of healthcare , you’ll find your purpose here.
Primary Function of Position
The Analyst, EFT Trade Compliance and Operations is responsible for overseeing and
coordinating all international movements originating from the United States to destinations
worldwide, including but not limited to Mexico, Germany, Bulgaria, and Malaysia. The scope
includes equipment, service parts, repairs, upgrades, returns, loaners, demonstrations,
manufacturing-related tools, components, and materials. This role serves as the primary
coordinator for the end-to-end Shipment Authorization Form (SAF) process and as the
operational interface among engineering, manufacturing, supply chain, procurement, logistics,
customs brokers, suppliers, and trade compliance. The position owns shipment visibility,
status management, escalation handling, regulatory readiness, classification
governance, permit management, and export/import compliance from submission through
U.S. export and destination-country import. It ensures products are properly classified,
registered, documented, and compliance-ready before shipment approval.
Essential Job Duties
 Manage end-to-end international movements of capital equipment, repairs, returns,
demonstration units, components, service parts, manufacturing-related tools, and
materials from the United States to countries worldwide
 Serve as the primary point of contact for international outbound movements from the
United States and related returns, and lead cross-functional escalation calls for critical
shipments.
 Manage active Shipment Authorization Form (SAF) requests, monitor shipment
milestones and readiness, and serve as the primary owner of the SAF Helpline Zoom
Channel.
 Provide shipment status updates to engineers and project teams, track open issues,
and ensure timely resolution.
 Coordinate with customs brokers, freight forwarders, and logistics providers to
support timely U.S. export and destination-country import clearance and resolve holds,
delays, documentation issues, and classification discrepancies.
 Manage U.S. export and destination-country tariff classification activities.
 Partner with engineering, manufacturing, supply chain, procurement, suppliers, and
trade compliance to obtain and evaluate technical information required for classification
and country of origin determinations.
 Review engineering drawings, Bills of Materials, product specifications,
materials, component information, and product functionality to support HTS, Schedule
B, ECCN, and country of origin determinations.
 Verify completion of classification, country of origin documentation, FTA eligibility, metal
certificates, permit or license approvals, and customs documentation readiness.
 Evaluate destination-country import requirements, including permits, product
registrations, labeling or conformity requirements, special regulations, and customs
restrictions.
 Coordinate product data required for applicable customs, inventory control, and trade
compliance systems.
 Ensure products are compliance-ready before shipment authorization and support
inventory registration requirements and customs record maintenance.
 Ensure accurate tracking of exported, imported, transformed, returned, scrapped, and
transferred goods.
 Prepare, review, and validate commercial invoices, export filings, permits, licenses,
certificates, temporary import/export documents, and country-specific customs
declarations.
 Ensure compliance with U.S. export requirements, destination-country import
regulations, applicable trade laws, sanctions and restricted-party requirements, and
company policies.
 Maintain complete, audit-ready trade records and ensure proper export documentation,
recordkeeping, and regulatory compliance.
 Support engineering, manufacturing, service, and supply chain teams with global trade
compliance requirements.
 Support tariff and export classification, country of origin determinations, and trade
program utilization.
 Participate in internal audits and government compliance reviews, perform trade
compliance due diligence and transaction reviews, and support audits and
investigations.
 Identify compliance risks, implement corrective actions, and define requirements for
new shipment types and destination countries.
 Develop and maintain SOPs, procedures, work instructions, playbooks, knowledge
repositories, and classification databases.
 Identify process improvement and automation opportunities and support
implementation of global trade technology solutions.
 Maintain SAF tracking dashboards and monitor SLA performance; report shipment
aging, cycle times, backlog, and escalation metrics.
 Perform other duties, tasks, and special projects as assigned.
Required Skills and Experience
 Minimum 5 years of experience in:
• U.S.-Mexico cross-border operations
• Customs compliance
• Import/export operations
• IMMEX program administration
 Fluent in English and Spanish (written and verbal).
 Experience preparing customs documentation and supporting customs audits.
 Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
 Advanced Excel and ERP system experience.
Preferred Skills and Experience
 Experience in the medical device, healthcare, pharmaceutical, or highly regulated
manufacturing industry.
 Experience with FDA-regulated products.
 Knowledge of USMCA and other free trade agreement requirements.
 Experience with SAP, GTS, Annex 24 software, or other customs compliance systems.
 Customs certifications or trade compliance credentials are a plus.
 Knowledge of:
• IMMEX Program
• Annex 24
• Annex 30
• U.S. Import Compliance
• U.S. Export Compliance
• Customs broker management
• Temporary import/export programs
Education & Training
 Bachelor's degree in engineering, international trade, customs administration, supply
chain, business, logistics, or a related field.
Working Conditions
Normal office conditions.
Travel required (<10%) – both domestic and international.

Position Overview
The Upstream Reimbursement Strategist is the architect of the organization’s long-range reimbursement and market access strategy across the U.S. product portfolio. This person is responsible for generating all strategies for all upstream programs and dovetailing those strategies with global market access for ex-U.S. projects. This role is the closest link to the clinical development team and serves as the primary strategic interface with HEOR, regulatory affairs, and health policy stakeholders.
Responsible for evidence generation strategy, CPT/HCPCS code pathway design, CMS payment policy analysis, and the global coordination of evidence that feeds both upstream regulatory submissions and downstream field execution tools. This person shapes the narrative for why a product deserves reimbursement and builds the data package to support it.
Core Responsibilities
CPT/HCPCS Code Strategy: Lead the strategy for new code applications, Category III code conversions, and descriptor modifications. Manage engagement with AMA CPT Editorial Panel, RUC, and HCPCS workgroups.
CMS Payment Policy Analysis: Conduct ongoing analysis of OPPS, PFS, and ASC payment policy. Prepare and submit CMS comment letters during rulemaking cycles. Monitor NT-APC, pass-through, and device payment category developments.
Global Evidence Coordination: Serve as the connective tissue between U.S. evidence needs and global HEOR and OUS markets. Dovetail U.S. upstream strategies with global market access to ensure alignment on ex-U.S. projects. Ensure evidence generation is sequenced to serve both U.S. regulatory/payer needs and ex-U.S. HTA submissions, coordinating timing and deliverables across jurisdictions.
Coverage & Reimbursement Strategy: Generate and own the reimbursement strategy for all upstream programs across the full product portfolio. Develop and maintain the strategic reimbursement roadmap from early pipeline through commercialization, including target product profiles (TPPs) and core value dossiers (CVDs) for pipeline assets. Identify coverage gaps, analyze competitive reimbursement positioning, recommend pathway strategies, and ensure strategic continuity as products progress through development milestones.
U.S. Value Plan Implementation Support: Play a supporting role to HEOR in ensuring the U.S. Market Access team has secured the database resources required to execute strategy and implement the recommendations set out in the U.S. Value Plan.
Competitive Intelligence: Monitor competitor reimbursement strategies, code applications, pass-through approvals, and coverage determinations. Translate competitive intelligence into actionable strategic recommendations.
Product Positioning & Message Alignment: Serve as the primary owner of product positioning in coordination with select downstream stakeholders, ensuring messaging is consistent across other stakeholders in the organization — particularly when producing publications such as burden of illness, cost-utility, and budget impact analyses.
Market Access Research: Lead market access research to support value messaging, including claims analyses and — where needed — coordination of payer interviews, provider interviews, and other primary research.
Shared Midstream Responsibility: Contribute to code acquisition execution, pre-launch payer engagement planning, and payment policy implementation activities in partnership with the Mid/Downstream Tactician.
Required
Health policy degree or similar
3-8+ years of progressive experience in medical device market access, health economics, reimbursement strategy, or related field (for manager level, 3+)
Deep working knowledge of CMS OPPS/PFS/ASC payment systems, APC mechanics, and facility payment methodology
Experience with CPT, , AMA Editorial Panel processes, and HCPCS coding pathways
Strong analytical skills with experience interpreting claims data, cost reports, and CMS rulemaking documents
Excellent written and verbal communication skills; ability to translate complex policy into strategic recommendations
Ability to work cross-functionally with clinical, regulatory, HEOR, and commercial teams
Preferred
Advanced degree (MPH, MBA, or equivalent; PhD or PharmD also welcome)
Familiarity with healthcare data platforms
Familiarity with HEOR models

The Senior Mechanical Engineer works in and/or leads cross-functional teams to maintain and improve the design, production, and service of the da Vinci® Surgical System.  They will determine root cause of complex problems with electro-mechanical components, manufacturing process, and system performance.  They will identify mechanical design and manufacturing process solutions to improve performance, cost, and reliability. Proven ability to identify issues, bring clarity and transparency, and lead a team effectively to appropriate product solutions
Comfortable with all phases of the product development lifecycle including design, implementation, debug, verification, qualification, and transfer to Manufacturing.
Proven proficiency at failure analysis
Demonstrated mechanical design and analysis skills, including statics, dynamics, kinematics, strength of materials and stress analysis
Strong understanding of component selection criteria and materials as they relate to design and manufacturability
Experience with design for reliability, manufacturability, and assembly
Comfortable operating machine shop, measurement and test equipment
Ability to communicate effectively (written, oral) across all levels and organizations
Ability to mentor other engineers
Ability to travel up to 10% time
A real excitement to learn and get to the bottom of tough technical problems

BSME required with 8+ years or MSME (preferred) with 5+ years of industry experience in developing commercial mechanical and electromechanical robotic products

Regulatory agency experience including UL, CE, and FDA approval processes

Primary Function of Position
As a member of the service manufacturing engineering team, you will work in a dynamic, fast-paced, and challenging environment. You will be responsible for supporting the production of Da Vinci Surgical Robotic systems by applying your knowledge of system engineering including electromechanical assemblies and software to perform failure analysis, repair, and test of our systems. Your goal will be to improve customer experience through improvements in reliability, manufacturing yield, and design improvements of these surgical systems.
Essential Job Duties
This position is a dynamic technical systems focused role that requires strong communication, problem solving, cross functional teamwork and ability to present and drive continuous improvement to processes, products, and systems.  Your primary responsibilities will include:
Create, maintain, and improve manufacturing processes and methods to perform failure analysis of returned parts, identifying root causes of failed products.
Performing failure analysis on PCBAs, electromechanical assemblies, and related components utilizing design documentation, manufacturing test data, software tools, and a variety of lab / bench equipment.
Identifying emerging failure trends through structured problem solving (DMAIC, 8D, Fishbone, 5 Why), data analysis, manufacturing data, yields, and statistical process control
Creating and leading data driven cross-functional engineering team meetings to address manufacturing issues.
Prevents issue reoccurrence by successfully driving continuous improvement learnings from root cause analysis within engineering and manufacturing environments.
Establish and perform IQ/OQ/PQ on equipment and fixtures. As well as execute validations on Manufacturing lines (PPQ).
Provide production line support for day-to-day engineering issues and advanced failure analysis support
Identify and implement continuous improvement projects with respect to customer experience including failure modes, repeated issues, problem not reproduced issues.
Required Skills and Experience
Strong troubleshooting mind set - an ability to methodically break down a system or process into subparts to identify failures and troubleshoot to a component level. Familiarity with 8D problem solving, Fishbone Diagraming, and the 5 Whys.
Minimum 5 years experience as design or manufacturing engineer supporting product with significant electromechanical content.
Sense of curiosity and a willingness to always dig deeper.
Ability to read electronic and mechanical schematics, assembly, and fabrication drawings.  Execute testing and data collection using Linux, Matlab, and other software toolsets.
Strong skills in problem solving and using Minitab/JMP, Python, SQL, Tableau and/or other SW tools for data analysis to identify root cause and drive corrective actions.
Required Education and Training
BS degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering/Science, or Mechanical Engineering.
MS degree in Engineering preferred.
Working Conditions
Ability to sit and stand for long periods of time
Ability to lift, and carry parts weighing up to 40 lbs
Ability to maneuver into spaces around robotic system
Preferred Skills and Experience
“Self-starter” attitude and comfort in a hands-on environment, where he/she can demonstrate an ability to work with other engineers to influence product and manufacturing design to improve reliability.
Experience in an ISO 13485, ISO 9001, or medical device manufacturing environment
Experience and proficiency in ERP, CRM, PLM software including SAP and Agile.
Experience with use of EE lab equipment including Oscilloscopes, Spectrum Analyzers, Power supplies, and Multimeters

title: Senior Technical Editor
description:

The problems we solve demand creativity, rigor, and collaboration. The work is challenging, but deeply meaningful—because every improvement we make has the potential to change a life.
If you’re ready to contribute to something bigger than yourself and help transform the future of healthcare , you’ll find your purpose here.
Primary Function of Position
Services Technical Publications provides the foundation for every procedure performed on Intuitive's advanced medical devices by the global Field Service team. Our content is authored in DITA and delivered through guided workflows, which progressively discloses content for field service technicians install, maintain, and repair Intuitive systems.
In this role, you will combine expert editing skills with strategic thinking to develop and implement a comprehensive quality metrics program. You will work directly with technical writers, product teams, and stakeholders to ensure that hardware and software documentation meets our highest standards for clarity, accuracy, consistency, and usability within guided, step-by-step workflows.
As an individual contributor with significant influence and authority, your success will be measured by your ability to drive quality improvements and positive outcomes through collaboration, coaching, and strategic program development—not through direct management, but through leadership and expertise.
Essential Job Duties
Edit hardware and software technical documentation for clarity, accuracy, consistency, voice, tone, and usability. Champion minimalist, task-based writing principles to ensure content serves the immediate needs of field service technicians. Work directly with authors and SMEs to improve content quality across the publication lifecycle.
Make edits directly in IXIA, our component content management system, collaborating with technical writers and subject matter experts through the review workflow to implement changes efficiently. Comfort navigating the system and driving content improvements end-to-end.
Develop and own a quality metrics program that establishes baselines, identifies improvement opportunities, and measures impact. Use data-driven insights to guide editorial strategy and demonstrate ROI of editing services.
Design and implement best practices for technical content quality. Create scalable processes, guidelines, and checklists that enable teams to self-serve and maintain consistency without bottlenecking editorial review.
Lead training and coaching initiatives. Educate writers on minimalism, task-based authoring, topic-based writing principles, style, and grammar standards. Establish regular office hours, workshops, or feedback sessions to build writer capability and confidence.
Configure and integrate content quality tools (Acrolinx, Congree, Grammarly, or similar) into the publication workflow. Recommend technology solutions that enhance quality without creating friction for authors.
Collaborate with cross-functional teams—including product, UX, localization, and publishing—to align on quality standards and resolve editorial challenges.
Required Skills and Experience
Bachelor’s degree or equivalent
7+ years of professional editing experience in technical communications, with demonstrated expertise editing DITA-authored content for both hardware and software products.
Deep expertise in minimalist and task-based, topic-based authoring approaches. Demonstrated ability to coach authors on these principles and evaluate content for adherence to minimalist standards.
Proficiency with IXIA or similar component content management systems (CCMS). Ability to navigate the system, make edits directly, and move content through review workflows independently.
Experience developing or implementing editorial guidelines, style guides, or content quality standards. Comfort with creating scalable, repeatable processes.
Proficiency with quality assurance tools such as Acrolinx, Congree, Grammarly, or equivalent. Ability to evaluate tools and troubleshoot configuration issues.
Proven ability to communicate clearly and concisely, both in written and spoken formats. Skill in explaining complex editorial feedback in a way that educates rather than demoralizes.
Experience working with metrics, data collection, or quality measurement. Comfort with analyzing trends and using data to support recommendations.
Ability to influence and drive outcomes without direct authority. Success collaborating with subject matter experts, product teams, and writers who may not report to you.
Preferred Skills and Experience
Experience with medical device, surgical instrument, or other regulated/high-stakes technical documentation.
Familiarity with content management systems, publishing workflows, or localization processes.
Experience training or coaching other writers or editors.
Understanding of how DITA-authored content serves guided workflows with progressive disclosure, and how editing decisions impact both user experience and compliance.

We’re a team of engineers, clinicians, and innovators united by one purpose: to make surgery smarter, safer, and more human. Every day, our work helps care teams perform with greater precision and patients recover faster, improving outcomes around the world.
The problems we solve demand creativity, rigor, and collaboration. The work is challenging, but deeply meaningful—because every improvement we make has the potential to change a life.
If you’re ready to contribute to something bigger than yourself and help transform the future of healthcare , you’ll find your purpose here.

Financial Modeling & Analysis
Lead the development, ownership, and enhancement of complex financial and valuation models to analyze economic merits, risks, pricing strategies, and returns for renewable, thermal, and transmission projects.

Identify commercial, economic, and structural risks and propose mitigation strategies to improve competitiveness and bankability.
Collaborate with advisors, consultants, trade groups, and legal counsel to refine assumptions, enhance models, and improve development strategies.
Communication, Leadership & Organizational Impact
Mentor and support junior CFE team members through expectation-setting, work review, feedback, and coaching.
Prepare clear, concise presentations and memos summarizing key findings, model insights, risks, and recommendations for senior leadership.
Deliver training to upskill internal teams on financial modeling, revenue structures, market dynamics, and project economics.
Lead or contribute to process improvement initiatives that strengthen modeling consistency, speed, and accuracy across the organization.

Bachelor’s degree in Business, Economics, Engineering, Accounting, Finance, or related field (Master’s preferred).
1+ years of experience in commercial, financial, or analytical roles in energy, infrastructure, utilities, banking, consulting, or real estate development.
Demonstrated ability to build, manage, audit, and interpret complex financial and economic models.
Strong analytical, problem-solving, and critical-thinking skills with the ability to communicate trade-offs and risk/reward balances.
Experience managing multiple projects and coordinating across cross-functional teams in fast-paced settings.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, especially in presenting financial topics to senior audiences.
Knowledge of budgeting, cost forecasting, project development processes, and financial oversight.
Advanced Excel skills (VBA, pivot tables, lookups, conditional logic, macros, scenario modeling) and strong Word/PowerPoint proficiency.
Preferred Qualifications:
Experience with project finance, infrastructure valuation, or utility-scale renewable, thermal, storage, or transmission development.
Demonstrated expertise in advanced financial modeling, including Monte Carlo simulations, debt sculpting, risk-weighted returns, power market modeling, and multi-technology valuation.
Proficiency with MATLAB and/or Python for simulations, optimization, scenario automation, data processing, and integration with Excel modeling frameworks.
Experience building standardized modeling templates, assumption libraries, or automated analysis tools.
Ability to synthesize complex economic impacts into clear summaries for leadership.
Strong organizational skills and the ability to manage numerous concurrent projects.
Self-starter with strong judgment and the ability to operate with minimal direction.
Strong interpersonal skills and confidence engaging senior managers, engineers, advisors, and multi-disciplinary teams.

As a Senior Staff Engineer, Renewable Electrical Engineering, you will serve as a proven individual contributor supporting the electrical engineering and construction of cutting-edge utility-scale renewable energy projects. Reporting to the Manager or Director, Electrical Engineering, and based on-site at Invenergy's downtown Chicago, IL office, you will take on increased accountability and ownership over basic and moderately complex electrical engineering tasks across the full project life cycle — supporting conceptual project designs and coordinating with selected engineering firms to advance final detailed designs for projects to be built.
You will exercise independent judgment within established engineering procedures and Invenergy's design standards, receiving minimal instruction on day-to-day work and general instruction on new assignments. Your work will require occasional process checks and review by a senior coworker or supervisor at critical milestones, and you will proactively communicate issues and findings to your manager as they arise. You will operate as a team member with no supervisory responsibilities over others, and your external interactions will be job-specific and limited in most cases.
The electrical systems of Invenergy's renewable energy projects utilize inverter-based wind and solar generators that include 1500V DC wiring systems, 34.5kV AC medium voltage collection and distribution circuits, collector substations to step-up power, and transmission line interconnections to the grid at high and extra high voltages.
Responsibilities
Engineering Design
Develop conceptual project designs within established engineering procedures and Invenergy's design standards, exercising judgment within defined guidelines to ensure designs reflect critical owner and interconnection requirements, with occasional review by senior engineers at key milestones.
Conduct design reviews of electrical drawings — including DC solar, AC collection systems for wind and solar, substation, and transmission line designs — exercising independent judgment within established review procedures, applying knowledge of fundamental engineering concepts, and communicating findings and discrepancies to senior engineers.
Support the definition of the scope of required electrical system studies, applying knowledge of professional concepts and established procedures, and assist in reviewing study results for accuracy and compliance, communicating questions and issues to senior engineers as they arise.
Track design schedules and update relevant internal stakeholders on the status of electrical engineering tasks, exercising judgment within established workflows to support on-time delivery of critical project milestones and communicating risks to management proactively.
Support project closeout by organizing and assisting in the transfer of all as-built documentation to the final project owner — including electrical drawings, schematics, bills of materials, electrical studies, and relay settings — within established project closeout procedures.
Procurement & Construction Support
Assist in reviewing competitive bids for owner-procured electrical materials, applying knowledge of fundamental engineering and procurement concepts, and support purchasing activities by coordinating with suppliers under general direction throughout the engineering and commissioning process, communicating issues to senior engineers as they arise.
Monitor construction progress remotely and via on-site inspections, exercising independent judgment within established procedures to identify field issues, support their resolution, and communicate findings and risks to senior engineers and management proactively.
Attend on-site meetings with electrical construction contractors and in-person coordination meetings with interconnection utilities in a job-specific and limited external interaction capacity, representing Invenergy professionally and escalating complex technical issues to senior engineers as appropriate.
Perform factory and equipment inspections and witness factory acceptance testing for major materials, exercising judgment within established inspection procedures and communicating findings to senior engineers.
Electrical Engineering Group Responsibilities
Assist in developing project-specific construction, engineering, and equipment specifications, applying knowledge of professional engineering concepts, policies, and procedures, and modifying standard approaches as appropriate based on project-specific requirements under general direction.
Prepare and validate electrical energy calculations, exercising independent judgment within established engineering methods and communicating questions, discrepancies, and findings to senior engineers as appropriate.
Participate in coordination with independent engineers and project partners in support of the technical due diligence process, in a job-specific and limited external capacity, escalating complex technical issues to senior engineers and management as appropriate.
Assist in the development of new projects by analyzing conceptual designs and RFQ specifications, applying knowledge of fundamental engineering concepts and modifying approaches based on project-specific requirements under general direction.
Coordinate with the Operations Engineering team to support the incorporation of lessons learned into new design reviews and specifications, exercising judgment within established workflows to apply relevant operational insights to assigned engineering tasks.
Maintain up-to-date knowledge of industry technology, power systems, and electrical engineering best practices through relevant training sessions, conferences, and professional development activities, applying new knowledge to assigned tasks and sharing relevant insights with the team.
Required Qualifications
Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering or a related technical discipline.
2–4 years of relevant work experience in electrical engineering, power systems, or a related field, including internships with a demonstrable transferable skillset.
Demonstrated experience with HV/MV electrical infrastructure — including substations and switchyards, distribution systems, transmission lines, and transformers — through relevant coursework, internships, or professional work experience.
Knowledge of power systems, acquired through specific coursework, internships, or professional work experience, with demonstrated ability to apply fundamental engineering concepts to moderately complex tasks.
Demonstrated ability to exercise independent judgment within established engineering procedures and policies, manage assigned moderately complex tasks with growing autonomy, and communicate issues and findings to management proactively.
General knowledge of interpreting and applying common electrical industry standards and codes.
Computer proficiency in Microsoft Excel, Word, and Visio.
Strong verbal and written communication skills with high attention to detail, ensuring technical work products and communications are accurate, concise, and professionally presented.
Some travel required (up to 25%).

Experience guiding architecture across complex ERP landscapes that include SAP and non-SAP platforms.
Demonstrated ability to influence cross-functional stakeholders and drive architecture decisions without direct authority.

Experience contributing to architecture standards, review processes, roadmaps, and reusable design patterns.
Strong communication skills, including the ability to present technical recommendations to both technical teams and senior non-technical stakeholders.

title: Part Time Sales Associate (Brick Specialist) Raleigh, NC
description:
Job Description
Part Time Sales Associate (Brick Specialist)
Are you excited to deliver inspirational retail experiences to LEGO® fans of all ages?
Join the LEGO® Brand Retail team as a Seasonal “Brick Specialist” and provide inspirational guest experiences in an interactive and vibrant store environment. We are looking for energetic, enthusiastic individuals to join us on a seasonal, part-time basis.
Exceed our guests’ expectations through fun and meaningful interactions
· Ensure a signature experience for every guest that visits our LEGO stores by greeting every guest in your location, performing all cash register functions and portraying a professional, gracious, friendly and engaging manner at all times (80%)
· Provide a clean, safe and visually stimulating environment by performing daily cleaning duties, maintaining store displays and learning and executing LEGO Brand Retail visual standards (10%)
· Safely and efficiently operate the store stockroom as you assist in the receiving of merchandise, maintain the stockroom to LBR standards, know and abide by all safety regulations and notify management of potential shortage situations (10%)
Deliver inspirational retail experiences built on LEGO Brand values
The LEGO® Group is a family-owned, international business and collaboration shapes everything we do. It’s all about a shared vision to launch inspiring products that will shape the future of play. You’ll be part of a uniquely creative organization that gives you the freedom to make a real impact on our performance — and have fun while you’re doing it. LEGO Brand Retail strives to foster relationships with our guests that transcend generations and are as timeless as the products we sell.
Do you have what it takes to inspire and develop the builders of tomorrow?
· Communicate effectively with team members and guests
· Process information/merchandise through the register system
· Work various hours, days, nights and weekends as business dictates
· Freely access all areas of the store including sales floor, stock areas, register areas, and loading dock area
· Physical specifications: Constant moving, talking, hearing, reaching, grabbing and standing for at least two consecutive hours. May occasionally involve stooping, kneeling, crouching, and climbing ladders. Vision abilities include close vision, depth perception, and ability to adjust focus. Involves lifting at least 30 lbs
· There is potential for this to become a regular role for excellent performers
We want you to join the LEGO Brand Retail team!
If you are confident that you have what it takes to succeed in this seasonal part-time role, use the APPLY NOW button above or below.
BRINGING IT TO LIFE
“The reason LEGO® exists is because of what they are doing for children around the globe. Everyone in the company, at all levels, feels privileged to be part of a company with such an inspiring vision” . VP of Operations in Americas & Pacific
Additional Details
We conduct drug screening as a part of our drug free workplace policy and in support of our commitment to the health and safety of our employees.
We are an equal opportunity employer and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability status, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law.

Family   Care   Leave –  We offer enhanced paid leave options for those important times.

Thank you for sharing our global commitment to Children’s Rights.
Just imagine building your dream career.
Then make it real.
Join the LEGO® team today.

title: Associate Director, Finance - Cash COE
description:
Job Description:
The Associate Director, Finance - Cash COE plays a critical role in driving cash excellence and delivering superior insights across Mars Snacking. Acting as a key strategic thought partner to the Segment CFO, Regional CFOs, and Global Segment Leaders, this role ensures that sophisticated cash analytics and deep financial insights translate directly into impactful, scaled initiatives. The Associate Director, Finance - Cash COE will lead the governance of global cash planning, forecasting, and reporting cycles, while aggressively driving process standardizations and pioneering the integration of advanced technologies and AI to unlock value creation and operational efficiency.
Candidate Profile & Experience
Experience: 7+ years of progressive experience in corporate finance, FP&A, or treasury within a large multinational FMCG or corporate environment.
Bachelor s degree in Finance, Business, Economics or a related field required
Domain Expertise: Deep technical knowledge of liquidity management, working capital drivers, cash flow statement mechanics, and corporate governance.
Technical & AI Savvy: Proven track record of leveraging modern finance tech (SAP, Power BI) and a strong curiosity for piloting and scaling generative AI tools.
Leadership & Standing: Exceptional stakeholder management skills with the confidence to influence, challenge, and align Regional CFOs, cross functional leaders, and corporate treasury peers.
Communication & Executive Presentation: Exceptional verbal and written communication skills—capable of cutting through complexity to deliver concise, actionable business recommendations directly to executive boards, including the ability to draft, structure, and deliver high-impact slides and presentations for senior leadership.

Cash Governance, Reporting, & Cycle Management
Strategic Oversight: Standardize, execute, and govern the global cash planning, forecasting, and reporting cycles across all Snacking business units.
Executive Delivery: Synthesize complex cash performance, liquidity risks, and balance sheet drivers into clear, high-impact narratives for the Segment CFO and executive leadership.
Process Integrity: Establish and enforce strict global cash governance standards, ensuring consistency, accountability, and accuracy in liquidity reporting.
2. Driving Excellence & Process Efficiency
Uncover areas within the business to drive performance improvements and value creation, leveraging data and advanced analytics techniques
Standardization: Move the organization from fragmented regional cash reporting to a highly standardized, centralized, and frictionless global operating model.
3. Strategic Insights Delivery & Capability Scaling
Help ensure that the deep insights generated through sophisticated analytics translate into actions and initiatives that have impact at scale in an organization, working closely with Segment leaders
Technological Capability Building: Collaborate with the Digital Technologies to deploy cutting-edge tools and build robust data pipelines, reducing the forecasting cycle time while drastically improving accuracy
Agentic Automation: Pioneer the use of Generative AI and automated agents to automate routine variance analysis, draft executive cash commentaries, and execute transactional data processing safely.

Job Description:
Digital Technology Product Lead – Digital and Agentic Commerce
At Mars Snacking, our purpose is to inspire happiness with better snacks for better days. Our iconic brands M&M'S®, PRINGLES®, SNICKERS®, CHEEZ-IT®, EXTRA®, Skittles®, POP-TARTS® and KIND® are enjoyed in more than 180 countries, sparking connection, creating memories, and adding a little brightness to everyday moments. As the world's leading maker of chocolate, gum, mints and fruity confections, we know that snacks may be small, but they carry real meaning, and behind every one is a team of passionate Associates working to make it even better.
Mars Snacking's Tech-Fueled Sales (TFS) ambition is to build a human-led, digitally powered Sales Engine that keeps our Associates at the center. Within TFS, cross-functional PODs operate as agile value engines, bringing together commercial experts, product leaders, process champions, and digital technologists to deliver high-impact capabilities directly into the flow of commerce. As consumer discovery and commerce continue to evolve through AI-powered experiences, conversational assistants, and emerging digital channels, Mars is helping shape the future of Digital and Agentic Commerce.
The Digital Technology Product Lead – Digital and Agentic Commerce serves as the Product Owner for Mars Snacking's global Digital Commerce and Agentic Commerce capabilities within Tech-Fueled Sales. Partnering closely with the Global DCom POD Lead, this role owns the product vision, roadmap, and delivery of solutions that connect Mars brands to emerging AI-powered shopping experiences, retailer ecosystems, and digital commerce platforms at global scale.
What Are We Looking For?
Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Business Administration, Product Management, or a related field.
5+ years of experience in digital product management, digital commerce, e-commerce, or related technology disciplines.
Proven success leading products from discovery and strategy through delivery, launch, and ongoing optimization.
Experience operating as a Product Owner within Agile/Scrum environments, partnering with engineering teams and business stakeholders.
Understanding of digital commerce ecosystems, including online marketplaces, retailer platforms, digital shelf capabilities, and transactional experiences.
Knowledge of APIs, data integrations, cloud technologies, and modern software development practices.
Familiarity with emerging AI technologies, agent-based systems, and generative AI applications in commerce.
Strong stakeholder management skills with the ability to influence and align cross-functional and executive audiences.
Experience working with external technology partners, vendors, and systems integrators.
Product management, Agile, cloud, or AI-related certifications preferred.

Define Product Strategy & Roadmap : Own and execute the multi-year roadmap for Digital Commerce and Agentic Commerce capabilities, balancing immediate business needs with long-term platform scalability.
Lead Agile Product Delivery : Partner with the Global DCom POD Lead to translate business priorities into product requirements, technical roadmaps, delivery plans, and sprint backlogs.

Ensure Platform Performance & Reliability : Define and uphold standards for security, scalability, availability, observability, and operational excellence across products.
Own End-to-End Product Operations : Oversee product lifecycle management, release readiness, adoption, monitoring, support transition, and continuous improvement activities.
Manage Strategic Technology Partners : Lead technical vendor engagements, solution evaluations, statements of work, and delivery governance to ensure high-quality outcomes.
Drive Innovation & Experimentation : Monitor emerging technologies and lead proof-of-concept initiatives to validate new Digital Commerce and AI-driven opportunities.
Support Global Deployment & Adoption : Design solutions for global scale while enabling regional and market-specific localization needs.

description:
Job Description:
HSE Manager -
Gainesville, GA
Champion safety, sustainability, and operational excellence.
As the   Site HSE Manager, you will lead and elevate our comprehensive Health, Safety, Environmental, and Security programs across the site. In this pivotal leadership role, you will safeguard our people, property, and assets while ensuring full regulatory compliance with OSHA, EPA, insurance, and corporate standards. By partnering closely with site teams, you will drive policy innovation, shape day-to-day HSE operations, and foster a proactive safety culture built on associate engagement and collaborative leadership.
What are we looking for?
Minimum
Bachelor’s degree in Occupational Safety & Health, Environmental Engineering/Science, Industrial Hygiene, or a related technical discipline.
10 - 15 years’ experience in implementing safety, environmental and/or industrial hygiene programs within manufacturing environment.
7+ years HSE leadership experience in a   manufacturing, supply chain, or industrial operations   environment.
Working knowledge of DOT regulations  for the handling and shipment of hazardous materials/waste.
Demonstrated experience managing comprehensive   environmental permit compliance   (Air, Stormwater, Wastewater, Spill Prevention/SPCC, and Hazardous Waste/RCRA).
Proven track record leading   incident investigations (Root Cause Analysis)   and implementing corrective/preventative action (CAPA) systems.
Hands-on experience with  Industrial Hygiene monitoring  (noise, ergonomics, respirable dust, chemical exposures) and occupational injury case management.
Experience evaluating  process safety hazards, combustible dust risks, and high-fire risk operations .
Demonstrated ability to  lead through influence  across all operational levels where direct reporting lines do not exist.
Experience managing contractor safety programs, emergency response teams (Site Emergency Organization), and physical site security operations.
Proficiency in  data-driven HSE management , using KPIs to prioritize resources, track performance, and report to senior leadership.
Preferred:
Master’s degree in HSE, Environmental Management, or related field.
Knowledge and experience in food manufacturing and GMP
Prior work experience managing security function
Professional certifications such as   CSP   (Certified Safety Professional),   CIH   (Certified Industrial Hygienist), or   CHMM   (Certified Hazardous Materials Manager).
Experience working within Total Productive Maintenance (TPM), Lean Manufacturing, or leading a   Safety Pillar / Continuous Improvement Pillar   (e.g., Mars Supply Excellence).
Expertise implementing and championing   Behavior-Based Safety (BBS)   programs and associate-led safety committees.
Background in   food manufacturing, CPG, or high-speed packaging   environments.
Familiarity with property loss control, asset conservation, and working with third-party insurance risk engineers (e.g., FM Global standards).
Experience managing operational budgets, capital project HSE reviews, and third-party integrated facilities/security teams.
What will be your key responsibilities?
Define the site’s HSE vision and lead as the   Safety Pillar Leader   (supporting TPM/MSE frameworks) to embed continuous improvement into daily manufacturing operations.

description:
Job Description:
ABOUT NATURE’S BAKERY
At Nature's Bakery, we believe simple, wholesome snacks are the best fuel for an active, joyful life. Founded in 2011 and now part of the Mars family, we are one of the fastest-growing snack brands. We bake delicious, plant-based, nut-free, and dairy-free bars using real ingredients like whole grains and fruit.
Job Description:
Nature’s Bakery is seeking a Senior Manager, Integrated Intelligence to serve as our lead consumer champion and strategic thought partner. In this role, you will connect human behavior, category dynamics, and cultural trends to actionable business strategies—ensuring the consumer remains at the heart of every brand, innovation, and commercial decision.
The ideal candidate is more than a research expert: you are a curious, business-minded leader who thrives in ambiguity, pairs hands-on research execution with high-level synthesis, and turns data into clear, compelling recommendations that drive sustainable growth across Marketing, Sales, and R&D.
What You’ll Do
Drive the Consumer Insights Agenda: Own and deliver a prioritized consumer & shopper learning roadmap aligned with critical business objectives, strategically managing research budgets, agency partners, and vendor selection.
Build Deep Consumer & Category Understanding: Establish an authoritative point of view on snack bar consumers, shoppers, eating occasions, cultural shifts, and competitive dynamics to inform brand positioning and portfolio growth.
Fuel the Innovation Pipeline: Partner closely with R&D and Brand Marketing from fuzzy front-end exploration through in-market launch—identifying whitespace, sizing unmet needs, validating claims and formulations, and translating food trends into actionable product concepts.
Lead Hands-On Primary Research & Brand Health: Personally design, execute, and analyze custom qualitative and quantitative studies (e.g., concept, pack, and creative testing) while tracking brand equity, consideration, and first-party consumer metrics.
Commercial Effectiveness & Media ROI: Serve as the insights thought partner for Marketing Mix Modeling (MMM) and media performance readouts, collaborating with media agencies and Finance to interpret channel ROI, saturation curves, and campaign lift to optimize spend.
Synthesize Multi-Source Data into Business Action: Connect primary research, syndicated scanner data, household panel data, and social listening into unified narratives that diagnose business performance and guide decisions across Sales, Marketing, and Executive Leadership.
What You’ll Bring:
Experience & Education
Education: Bachelor’s degree in Marketing, Business Analytics, Consumer Psychology, Economics, Statistics, or a related discipline required; Master’s/MBA is a plus.
Experience: 5+ years of progressive consumer insights / market research experience within CPG/FMCG (food and beverage experience strongly preferred).
Environment Agility: Proven track record thriving in an entrepreneurial, fast-paced environment with lean budgets, combined with the strategic acumen to navigate enterprise-scale business questions.
Technical & Methodological Competencies
Custom Research Craft: Hands-on mastery of the entire research lifecycle—including screener and questionnaire writing, vendor scoping, qualitative moderation, and statistical interpretation.
Syndicated & Panel Fluency: Proficient in interrogating syndicated retail scan data (Circana / NielsenIQ) and consumer household panels (Numerator).
Commercial Analytics Literacy: Practical ability to interpret Marketing Mix Modeling (MMM) outputs, attribution models, and media performance indicators to inform marketing budget decisions.
Digital & Emerging Tools: Exposure to modern research tech stacks, including social listening tools, agile digital testing platforms, and first-party survey tools.
Leadership & Behavioral Attributes
Strategic Influencer: Ability to distill complex, ambiguous data into a clear point of view with actionable recommendations for senior leadership.
Player-Coach Mentality: Unafraid to roll up sleeves to do the direct research work while serving as a strategic advisor to cross-functional partners.
Strong Communicator: Outstanding narrative storytelling and presentation skills that inspire cross-functional teams to take action.

title: Senior Director, Strategic Initiatives – Better For You
description:
Job Description:
Who are we?
Accelerator, a global Division of Mars Snacking, is on the front line of unlocking growth across high-potential categories and brands to fuel what’s next for Snacking. It’s home to both emerging and enduring brands, including KIND, TRÜ FRÜ, NATURE’S BAKERY, RXBAR, EGGO, POP-TARTS and RICE KRISPIE TREATS. Combining the scale of Mars with the agility of a start-up, our Division has the ambition to accelerate the future of snacking by delivering products consumers love today, discovering category-shaping innovations for tomorrow and developing entrepreneurial teams whose impact will last for generations.
We’re looking for passionate talent who dare to dream big, agile collaborators who talk straight and decide fast, and driven performers with a growth mindset. We’re proudly part of Mars, while also building something boldly different. If this inspires and energizes you, you’ve found the right place where you can do cool things with fun people for one of the biggest snacking companies in the world!
What will you do?
Reporting to the General Manager, Better-For-You (BFY), the Sr. Director, Strategic Initiatives serves as a key architect of the BFY business strategy and operating agenda. The Better-For-You portfolio includes KIND, RX, Pure Organic, Nutri-Grain, Special K Bars, and Kashi Bars across North America (US and Canada), spanning founder-led insurgency brands through scaled growth platforms. This role partners across Commercial, Supply, Finance, R&D, Strategy, and Enterprise functions to identify, prioritize, and deliver the initiatives that create sustainable growth and improve overall business performance.
As a member of the Better For You Leadership Team, this leader drives Business Unit and enterprise-wide strategic priorities, coordinating complex cross-functional initiatives, accelerating decision-making, and ensuring the organization remains focused on the highest-value opportunities of today and the future. Success requires a unique combination of strategic thinking, business acumen, influence, organizational leadership, and execution excellence.
What would be your key responsibilities?
Shape and Drive the Better For You Growth Agenda
Partner with the General Manager and Leadership Team to develop and refine the BFY portfolio's multi-year growth strategy.
Identify strategic choices and steppingstones within brands, across portfolio and innovation, and among channels / customers,
Translate strategy into actionable business priorities, roadmaps, investment recommendations, and measurable outcomes.
Drive near term performance while maintaining an eye toward future-back trends / disruptions (consumer, regulatory, ecosystem) that will impact Snacking.
Lead Enterprise Strategic Initiatives
Own a portfolio of high-priority business initiatives that require cross-functional leadership and enterprise coordination.
Serve as the leadership team's quarterback for transformational programs, business integrations, capability builds, and operating model improvements.
Drive disciplined execution, governance, risk management, and issue resolution across strategic initiatives.
Ensure critical projects remain on schedule, deliver expected outcomes, and generate measurable business impact.
Partner Across the Business to Improve Performance
Collaborate closely with Brand, Sales, Customer, Supply Chain, Finance, R&D, and Strategy to deliver the full potential of the business and supporting value creation algorithm (growth, P&L shape, and earnings position).
Diagnose business challenges and opportunities through data-driven analysis and prepare fact-based recommendations.
Facilitate dynamic resource allocation and investment decisions across competing business priorities.
Support annual planning, long-range planning, and portfolio reviews.
Drive Leadership Team Effectiveness
Partner with the General Manager to establish leadership team priorities, meeting effectiveness, decision-making processes, and execution rhythms.
Ensure alignment across the leadership team on strategic priorities, actions, accountabilities, and performance outcomes.
Facilitate cross-functional problem-solving and accelerate resolution of complex organizational issues.
Improve organizational focus by simplifying priorities and eliminating low-value activities.
Build Organizational Capabilities for Long-Term Success
Identify capability gaps that could constrain future growth and develop plans to address them.
Lead efforts to strengthen organizational effectiveness, ways of working, and cross-functional collaboration.
Support development of the BFY culture, employee engagement strategy, and leadership effectiveness initiatives.
Champion a culture of accountability, learning, agility, and continuous improvement.
Serve as a Strategic Advisor to the General Manager
Act as a trusted thought partner to the General Manager on business performance, organizational health, strategic choices, and change management.
Lead special projects, board-level analyses, executive presentations, and business reviews.
Prepare recommendations and materials for senior leadership discussions and key enterprise forums.
Represent the BFY business in cross-segment and enterprise strategic initiatives when appropriate.

title: Art Director, Business Marketing
description:
About the Team

Business Marketing helps knowledge workers, developers, and business decision-makers understand and adopt OpenAI’s products, supporting both self-serve growth and our managed sales team. Our creative work makes complex capabilities clear, grounded, and human as they move from the lab into businesses and everyday work.

About the Role

We’re looking for an experienced Art Director to develop and direct creative for OpenAI’s business audiences. You’ll turn product capabilities, customer insights, and marketing briefs into visual ideas that can carry a campaign across channels. That might mean developing the visual concept for a launch, storyboarding a film about how a customer uses AI in their work, or building a campaign system that holds together across a landing page, paid social, and a keynote.

This is a hands-on role. You’ll sketch concepts, build key visuals, and set the visual direction for designers, producers, and external partners. You’ll work closely with writers, Business Marketing, Product Marketing, and product teams to make sure the work is accurate, useful to the audience, and unmistakably OpenAI.

To us, creativity is a team sport. Ideas get better when you talk them through and build on each other’s thinking. We value curiosity over certainty, kindness over ego, and the ability to balance craft with decisiveness.

In this role, you will:

 - Lead visual concept development and art direction for B2B campaigns, product launches, customer stories, and industry events, from brief through final production.

 - Partner with writers and marketers to define the idea around a specific audience, what they need to understand, and what we want them to do next.

 - Work with product and technical partners to show how capabilities work in practice, using product imagery, demos, diagrams, and motion without overstating what the technology can do.

 - Develop campaign visual systems that adapt to different formats and audience needs, from a launch film or event keynote to a product page, paid campaign, or sales presentation.

 - Art direct photography, illustration, motion, and video. Make work yourself when the project calls for it, and give clear direction to internal teams and external partners when others are producing it.

 - Maintain a high visual bar across touch points and help evolve how the OpenAI brand shows up for business audiences.

You might thrive in this role if you:

 - Have 8+ years of art direction or related creative experience in-house, at an agency, or both, with a portfolio that shows your role in developing concepts and taking them through production.

 - Have experience creating work for business or technical audiences, with examples of making a complex product, service, or idea clear and compelling.

 - Bring strong visual design fundamentals in typography, composition, imagery, and systems, and can apply them across digital, social, film, and experiential work.

 - Can build a strong campaign idea and show how it adapts across formats without losing what makes it distinctive.

 - Can explain your creative decisions to marketing and product partners, work through feedback, and make sound tradeoffs when priorities or timelines change.

Nice to Have

 - Experience with AI, enterprise software, developer tools, or other emerging technologies.

 - Experience art directing customer stories, product demos, or keynote and event creative.

 - Motion design, video art direction, or on-set experience.

We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. AI is an extremely powerful tool that must be created with safety and human needs at its core, and to achieve our mission, we must encompass and value the many different perspectives, voices, and experiences that form the full spectrum of humanity.

description:

The Growth team helps people and businesses discover, adopt, and get lasting value from ChatGPT and other OpenAI products. We partner with Brand Marketing, Product, Engineering, Data Science, Finance, and Creative to connect marketing investment with customer and business outcomes. Our brand data infrastructure brings together media, audience, creative, and research data so teams can plan, measure, and improve brand investment across markets.

About the Role

We’re looking for a Brand Data Infrastructure Lead to own the data foundations that make brand marketing measurable and scalable. You will define how brand media, campaign, creative, audience, and research data are organized, connected, validated, and made available for decisions. This hands-on role combines brand and media expertise with practical data fluency, turning fragmented platform and partner outputs into dependable datasets and repeatable workflows.

This role sits within Growth Marketing and works closely with Brand Marketing, Media Operations, Growth Platform’s solutions engineering team, Data Engineering, and Data Science. You own Brand’s data roadmap, business definitions, source requirements, data-quality acceptance, and adoption. Engineering partners own production architecture, connector and pipeline implementation, instrumentation, and technical incident resolution. Data Science owns statistical methodology and model development.

Your first priority is to establish consistent campaign and creative taxonomies, dependable media and measurement feeds, clear data-sharing arrangements, and trusted reporting inputs. Build a foundation that supports TV/CTV, online video, social, audio, out-of-home, and other brand channels, with the coverage and history needed for brand tracking, lift studies, incrementally, and marketing mix modeling.

In this role, you will:

 - Own the Brand data infrastructure roadmap. Translate brand strategy, media plans, and measurement needs into prioritized data capabilities, source integrations, quality improvements, and reporting foundations. Balance business value, global coverage, delivery dependencies, cost, and sustained adoption.

 - Define shared data models and taxonomies. Establish consistent campaign, creative, channel, partner, audience, and market definitions, identifiers, reporting grains, and time conventions. Align stakeholders on how datasets connect and how metrics should be interpreted across platforms and markets.

 - Set source and integration requirements. Define the fields, granularity, history, coverage, refresh cadence, and reconciliation needed from platforms, agencies, publishers, and measurement vendors. Work with Data Science on study requirements and comparability, and connect media and research outputs with relevant product and business outcomes.

Use source reports and delivered datasets to identify missing feeds, taxonomy gaps, duplication, and reporting discrepancies; assess business impact, coordinate resolution, and validate recovery with the accountable technical or vendor owner.

 - Build usable data products and handoffs. Partner with data and analytics teams on curated Brand datasets, reporting inputs, documentation, and self-service access. Maintain definitions, lineage, training, and support procedures so Brand leaders, regional teams, and measurement specialists can use the data consistently with less manual reconciliation.

You might thrive in this role if you:

 - Bring 8+ years of experience in marketing data, brand or media measurement, marketing technology, analytics operations, or related roles, including hands-on ownership of data capabilities that improved marketing decisions.

 - Understand data models, identifiers, taxonomy, data contracts, and quality checks, and how they support brand lift, incrementality, and marketing mix modeling. You can interpret source extracts and reporting outputs, investigate discrepancies, and work effectively with measurement specialists.

description:
About the Team

Customer Education helps customers build the practical skills and confidence to use AI and OpenAI products safely and effectively. We bring together customer insight, learning and enablement expertise, product signals, and measurement to help organizations move from access to durable adoption.

Within Customer Education, the Certification team helps individuals demonstrate competence for in-demand AI skills and helps customers and partners validate that their workforce has the skills they need to meet their AI-enabled business goals. Similarly, Enterprise leaders should understand what each credential signifies and how it supports workforce readiness. We do this with transparency for the overall OpenAI credential framework and providing trusted, role-based certifications that verify practical capability.

About the Role

As a Certification Assessment Specialist, you will design, build, test, launch, and maintain the hands-on assessments behind an OpenAI technical role-based certification. Your work will help candidates demonstrate what they can do in realistic scenarios and give reviewers reliable evidence to score their work.

This is a hands-on individual contributor role reporting to the Technical Certification Lead. You will turn competency models, assessment blueprints and scoring rubrics into working tasks, assessment environments and workflows that capture candidate evidence and produce results reviewers can verify. You will use scripting and automation and partner with engineering on software development and delivery integrations.

You will work with the certification, measurement, engineering and operations teams, as well as technical subject matter experts and external delivery providers. The Technical Certification Lead will coordinate alignment with learning content while keeping confidential assessment details separate from learning materials.

You will take assessments from prototype through pilot, launch, and ongoing maintenance across live and virtual delivery. As products and tools change, you will update tasks, environments, and scoring together so candidates are assessed against the intended skills.

Success means candidates have the opportunity to demonstrate the competencies required for the certification, and reviewers can consistently score that work using evidence they can trace back to the submission.

In this role, you will:

 - Translate assessment blueprints into realistic scenarios, candidate instructions, and hands-on tasks. Work with subject matter experts to check that the tasks reflect the job and elicit the appropriate evidence for each rubric.

 - Define assessment environment requirements and build or configure the environments candidates will use. Establish repeatable provisioning and reset workflows for accounts, tools, data, and permissions so candidates start from consistent conditions.

 - Build and maintain pipelines that capture candidate submissions and other scoring evidence, apply scoring rules, and route results for review. Make scores traceable to the underlying evidence and protect sensitive data under approved controls.

 - Build and test model-assisted scoring with qualified human reviewers using established validation criteria. Compare model scores with calibrated expert judgments, investigate disagreements, implement agreed rules for routing cases to human review, and rerun validation tests after material changes to the model, task, or rubric.

 - Test assessments end to end, from environment setup to evidence capture and scoring. Use dry runs and pilots to check instructions, timing, accessibility, and failure recovery; fix defects and verify the fixes before release. Test scoring against multiple valid approaches, partial and incorrect submissions, and failures in the assessment environment, so a platform issue isn’t mistaken for a candidate error.

 - Translate assessment needs into requirements for delivery integrations. Partner with engineering and delivery providers to test candidate access, submission and results handoffs and troubleshoot issues.

 - Prepare assessments for launch with platform and operations partners. Document setup, version dependencies, and troubleshooting so delivery teams can run assessments consistently and respond when something breaks.

 - Maintain versioned tasks, environments, scoring configurations, and test fixtures. Use candidate feedback and delivery and scoring data to identify issues, update or retire tasks, and check that changes preserve the intended skills and difficulty.

 - Investigate technical issues raised during delivery or candidate review. Reproduce defects where possible, document what was affected, and test fixes with the relevant delivery partners.

You might thrive in this role if you:

 - Have personally designed and built performance-based, hands-on assessments, labs or simulations for technical roles, such as software developers or solution architects, and taken them through testing, launch and maintenance. Experience creating question-and-answer tests alone does not meet this requirement.

 - Have used scripting and automation to build and troubleshoot technical assessment environments. You can work with technical subject matter experts to translate realistic solutions into assessments; deep AI-engineering expertise or prior experience with a particular language or delivery platform is not required.

 - Have experience working at a technology company in a fast-paced environment, setting priorities and delivering work amid changing requirements and evolving business needs.

 - Can use a blueprint and rubric to design realistic tasks and specify what evidence distinguishes competent performance from task completion.

 - Have built or maintained workflows that capture submissions, process evidence, and produce traceable scores or reviewer outputs.

 - Have implemented or validated model-assisted scoring or evaluation against expert human judgments, and can explain when a score should go to human review.

 - Have worked directly with external technical experts or delivery providers and can translate requirements into integrations you can test end to end.

 - Have used pilot results, candidate feedback, and scoring or delivery data to improve assessment quality.

 - Understand how to build for accessibility and protect candidate evidence and confidential assessment content.

 - Communicate technical tradeoffs clearly to subject matter experts, measurement specialists, platform engineers, and operations teams.

It’s a plus if you have experience:

title: Data Scientist, Integrity
description:
ABOUT THE TEAM

OpenAI’s Integrity team protects people and businesses using ChatGPT, Codex, and the API from fraud, abuse, and harmful misuse. Our work spans payment and promotional abuse, compromised accounts and API credentials, business and advertiser integrity, and emerging misuse of frontier AI capabilities. We also help product teams measure authentic usage so that abuse doesn’t distort decisions about how our products are growing.

Integrity Data Science helps teams decide where to intervene and whether those interventions work. A payment control can prevent fraud while blocking legitimate purchases. A product launch can make it easier for customers to get started while creating new opportunities for abuse. We measure both sides of those decisions.



ABOUT THE ROLE

As a Data Scientist on Integrity, you’ll find emerging abuse patterns, size their impact, and lead the analytical work behind decisions about detection, enforcement, and product launches. You’ll work with Product, Engineering, Research, Policy, and Operations to turn findings into improvements and measure what happens after they ship.

 - Investigate anomalous activity across products. Estimate how common a problem is, who is affected, and what it costs users or the business. Use that evidence to recommend where to focus.

 - Define outcome metrics and guardrails, establish baselines, and build monitoring that surfaces changes in abuse, customer friction, and operational performance.

 - Help build and evaluate detection rules, classifiers, and human review workflows. Use labeled samples and review outcomes to understand what the systems miss, where they flag legitimate activity, and how those errors vary across users and products.

 - Design randomized holdouts and use quasi-experimental or observational methods when randomization is impractical. Estimate harm or fraud losses prevented alongside effects on legitimate users, revenue, compute costs, and review workload. Recommend whether to launch, expand, adjust, or retire a control.

 - Trace where signals, review decisions, or enforcement actions break down. Work with partners to close gaps and build reusable datasets, analyses, and investigation tools.



IDEAL CANDIDATE

 - You use AI tools to investigate large, messy datasets, test hypotheses quickly, and automate recurring analyses. You’re fluent in SQL and Python and can verify AI-generated queries, code, and conclusions against the underlying data.

 - You have strong statistical judgment and experience with experimentation, causal inference, or observational analysis. You can reason from incomplete or biased labels and explain how uncertainty affects a decision.

 - You take ownership of open-ended problems, from deciding what to measure through recommending an action and checking whether it worked.

 - You communicate clearly with technical and nontechnical partners and can explain the tradeoffs behind a recommendation.

 - Experience in integrity, trust and safety, fraud or risk analytics, security analytics, or applied ML evaluation is helpful. Experience evaluating detection systems, human review, or LLM-based classifiers is a plus.

description:
About the Team

OpenAI’s Robotics team builds hardware and software for general-purpose robots. We work closely with AI researchers and use what we learn from testing on physical robots to guide the next design.

About the Role

We’re hiring an Engineering Manager to lead engineers working on firmware, low-level controls, and systems software for onboard compute. You’ll develop the people doing this work and shape the roadmap with technical leads and partners in hardware and research. You’ll stay close enough to the engineering to help the team make difficult calls, whether that means running one more experiment on the bench or deciding that a change is ready to ship.

In this role, you will:

 - Hire and coach engineers, give them clear feedback, and help them grow. Give experienced engineers room to lead designs and create opportunities for others to take on technical ownership.

 - Set priorities with technical leads and partners in hardware and research. Decide how to staff the work, communicate tradeoffs early, and resolve dependencies that could hold up a hardware milestone.

 - Guide work on embedded systems, from board bring-up and device interfaces to actuator control. Invest in reusable systems software so other engineers can integrate hardware, command it, and understand how it responds.

 - Set the bar for changes that ship to physical robots. Use design reviews, hardware-in-the-loop tests, and measurements of timing, tracking accuracy, and fault recovery to judge readiness.

 - Bring the right people together when a problem crosses disciplines. If an actuator misses its target under load, help the team choose the measurement that will distinguish a controls problem from a firmware or mechanical one.

You might thrive in this role if you:

 - Have managed a team that shipped and supported software on physical hardware. You can point to engineers you hired or coached who went on to lead significant work of their own.

 - Bring depth in firmware, embedded operating systems, or real-time controls, and can reason across all three. Experience integrating custom hardware or off-the-shelf robotic platforms is valuable.

 - Have taken a robotic or electromechanical system from prototype through repeated use. You know when a quick bench test will answer a design question and when reliability needs to be demonstrated under load.
