title: Manufacturing Quality Engineer, Data Center Modular Builds
description:
About the Team

OpenAI and its capital and technology partners are building a global network of data centers for demanding AI workloads. The Infrastructure Quality team sets and verifies quality, reliability, and performance requirements for equipment across that network.

We work with manufacturing partners, general contractors, engineers, and operations staff from supplier qualification through commissioning. Together, we verify that equipment arrives ready for installation, startup, and long-term service.

About the Role

As a Manufacturing Quality Engineer for Data Center Modular Builds, you will own supplier manufacturing and integration quality for modular systems, including hot aisle containment (HAC), modular cooling units (MCUs), and electrical skids. Working with mechanical and electrical integrators and their suppliers, you will lead supplier qualification, support product and process development, and translate engineering requirements into manufacturing controls, inspections, and acceptance criteria.

You will partner with cross-functional teams to monitor production and integration quality, conduct audits, and resolve risks to integrated products acceptance and delivery. You will also serve as the primary quality contact for site escalations involving manufacturing or integration defects in modular systems and(OFCI) components. Through structured root-cause investigations, corrective action, and closed-loop learning (CLL), you will drive resolution and feed field lessons back into supplier processes to prevent recurrence and improve future builds.

Key responsibilities

Modular Systems Quality and Supplier Development

 - Lead supplier qualification and support product and process development for mechanical and electrical integrators.

 - Oversee manufacturing and integration quality for modular builds, including HACs, MCUs, and electrical skids.

 - Work with integrators and suppliers to translate engineering requirements and critical-to-quality (CTQ) characteristics into practical manufacturing controls, inspection points, and acceptance criteria.

 - Develop and drive supplier improvement plans (SIPs) using the Plan-Do-Check-Act (PDCA) approach to strengthen manufacturing and integration processes.

 - Use production data, audit findings, test results, and supplier scorecards to identify systemic or recurring issues, prioritize improvements, and measure sustained results.

Site Escalations and Corrective Action

 - Serve as the primary quality point of contact for escalated site issues attributable to manufacturing and integration failures, coordinating containment and resolution with site teams and supplier factories.

 - Lead root-cause and corrective-action (RCCA) investigations using structured methods such as 8D and 5 Whys. Verify root causes, track corrective and preventive actions to closure, and confirm their effectiveness.

 - Apply closed-loop learning (CLL) to incorporate field findings and lessons learned into supplier and integrator manufacturing controls and future builds, preventing recurrence.

Manufacturing and Integration Monitoring

 - Partner with Quality Program and Manufacturing Operations teams to monitor production and integration progress, quality controls, inspection results, and factory test readiness. Identify emerging risks and coordinate timely action with suppliers.

 - Conduct product and process audits during and after manufacturing and integration to verify compliance with engineering requirements, approved procedures, and quality standards. Document findings and track corrective actions to closure.

 - Align production checkpoints, inspections, and factory testing requirements with suppliers, engineering, sourcing, supply chain, commissioning, and quality teams. Coordinate deviation resolution and escalate risks to equipment acceptance or delivery.

Qualifications

 - Bachelor’s degree in electrical, mechanical, or industrial engineering.

 - At least 10 years of data center industry experience spanning quality engineering and manufacturing engineering.

 - Experience working with integrators and suppliers across multiple tiers to manage quality throughout the product lifecycle, from OFCI component manufacturing through integration and site issue resolution, and drive product and process improvements.

 - Ability to define CTQs and acceptance criteria, develop inspection and test checklists, review test results, and maintain auditable quality records.

 - Experience monitoring supplier production, conducting product and process audits, managing controlled documents and deviations, and using supplier scorecards to drive improvement.

 - Demonstrated experience leading root-cause investigations and corrective actions for manufacturing or field issues using structured methods such as 8D and 5 Whys, and driving continuous improvement through PDCA.

 - Ability to coordinate supplier schedules and plan inspections and tests across multiple equipment programs.

 - Ability to communicate quality requirements, resolve issues, and coordinate decisions across suppliers, engineering, commissioning, sourcing, supply chain, manufacturing, operations, and construction teams.

 - Willingness and ability to travel approximately 40% of the time to supplier manufacturing facilities and data center project sites.

Preferred Skills

 - Technical knowledge of data center infrastructure, including mechanical, electrical, and controls systems.

 - Experience in supplier performance management for mission-critical facilities.

 - ASQ Certified Quality Engineer, Quality Manager, or Quality Auditor.

 - Experience in industrial or high-volume manufacturing environments.

As Technical Certification Lead, you will lead the design, development, and ongoing quality of OpenAI’s technical role-based certifications. Your work will make clear what each certification validates and what candidates must demonstrate to earn it.

This is a hands-on people manager role on the Certification team. You will align learning content to competency models and blueprints while keeping confidential assessment content separate from learning development.

You will take certifications from role analysis through pilot, launch readiness, and ongoing maintenance. As AI tools and technical roles evolve, you will keep the assessments relevant to the work people actually do.

Success means each certification makes a clear claim about what someone can do, the assessment supports that claim, and the curriculum gives candidates a practical way to build the skills they need.

 - Build and maintain competency models and facilitate job-task analyses for technical roles. Work with practitioners and subject matter experts (SMEs) to identify critical tasks, define the skills and proficiency each role requires, and keep the models current.

title: Strategy & Operations, Marketing & Creative - MBA
description:
ABOUT QUINCE
Quince is a destination for builders, creators, innovators, and operators who want to come together and challenge the status quo. Our mission is simple: make really high quality essentials for really low prices, fairly and sustainably. We deliver on that mission through a unique manufacturer-to-consumer (M2C) model eliminating the layers of traditional retail that add cost and result in consumers paying more than they need to. We find, build relationships with, and work directly with the manufacturing partners behind some of the world’s finest products. From there, our teams design smart, efficient operational processes  and build and deploy proprietary technology, AI, and analytics to help us scale fast.
What began with a small assortment of elevated basics has quickly grown into a cross-category brand spanning apparel, accessories, home goods, and more. Today, tens of millions of people across a growing number of countries come – and return – to Quince because they trust us to deliver.
OUR CULTURE
Quince is a culture built for builders by builders. Our way of working starts with a blank sheet of paper. We question conventional thinking, use technology and data to uncover new opportunities, and move quickly to turn ideas into reality. We aren’t interested in replicating how others do retail. We’re building a better way – at a speed and scale unlike anything that’s been done before.
We dream big and chase the hard problems others shy away from. Rejecting long-held assumptions is part of our company's DNA.  Where conventional wisdom says you have to choose – soft or durable, speed or rigor, quality or price – we ask why that trade-off has to exist in the first place.
Our pace is fast and the bar is high because our customers expect a lot from us and we refuse to let them down. We believe the best results come from challenging ourselves, learning from one another, and building on each other's strengths.
Here, responsibility is not determined by role, tenure, or seniority. Every team member - no matter their level - has the opportunity to drive our business and shape our trajectory.
If you’re someone who likes to imagine new possibilities and build better systems rather than plug-in to outdated ones, Quince is the place for you.
THE ROLE
Strategy & Operations, Marketing & Creative - MBA
Marketing & Creative shapes how customers discover Quince and how the brand shows up. We are seeking a Strategy & Operations Lead, Marketing & Creative to connect performance analytics with brand and creative strategy, helping grow our customer base efficiently. You will own growth initiatives, partner with creative teams on campaigns and content, and test what drives stronger acquisition, retention and conversion. Your work will turn insights into decisions about how we reach customers and where we invest. This role is based in our Palo Alto office, four days per week in office. The estimated start date will be June/July 2027. Candidates are welcome to apply to more than one Quince MBA role.
Strategy & Operations Leads help run the business inside their function. You will partner with senior leaders to set strategy, own initiatives end to end, and learn what it takes to build and scale a business inside a rapidly growing company.
A launchpad to entrepreneurship: operate as a core member of your team, roll up your sleeves and make an immediate, measurable impact across the business.
An accelerated growth path: work hand in hand with leaders across the company, take on a big scope, tackle complex problems and develop into a leader who knows how to build a business and grow a P&L.
Depth with purpose: own strategic initiatives that require you to go deep into the business. An obsession with the details is where the most meaningful breakthroughs come from.
Responsibilities
Own growth initiatives across paid, lifecycle/CRM and emerging channels
Analyze acquisition, retention and channel performance (CAC, ROAS, LTV) to guide budget and spend-mix decisions
Partner with creative teams on campaigns, content and brand strategy
Design and run tests to improve messaging, targeting and conversion
Work with merchandising on product launches and seasonal campaigns
Qualifications
Required:
3-6 years of prior professional experience in consulting, investment banking, private equity, tech, retail or related fields
Strong analytical, problem-solving, and communication skills
Ability to operate in ambiguity and bring structure to new problem sets
Comfort in a fast-paced, entrepreneurial environment
Comfort with marketing analytics and experimentation
Preferred:
Experience in growth or brand marketing, e-commerce or consumer tech
Direct-to-consumer or retail background
Interest in creative strategy and brand building
Pay Range: $175,000 - 200,000
All posted ranges are reflective of base salary and may vary depending upon experience level and location.   Bonus and equity may also be provided for eligible roles.
WHY QUINCE?
Joining Quince means being part of a mission-driven team reshaping retail. You will work alongside talented colleagues, tackle meaningful challenges, and contribute to building a more sustainable, accessible future for customers and partners alike.

title: Staff Service Engineer, Body Structures
description: About Rivian Rivian is on a mission to keep the world adventurous forever. This goes for the emissions-free Electric Adventure Vehicles we build, and the curious, courageous souls we seek to attract. Role Summary The Collision Repair Service Engineer is responsible for defining collision repairability and service strategies for all body sheet metal components from the earliest stages of new vehicle development through launch and 3rd level field support. This role represents the voice of the collision repair technician, customer, insurer, and certified repair facility in vehicle design decisions, helping Rivian deliver vehicles that are safe, insurable, repairable, and economically viable to restore after a collision. The engineer will leverage RCAR principles, collision repair industry practices, organizational feedback, and service engineering expertise to influence design concepts before key architecture and component decisions are finalized. The role will simplify repair strategies for complex vehicle structures, establish repair-versus-replace recommendations, create service part numbers and if necessary drawings for service unique subassemblies, and own the service bill of materials to enable sourcing for our NPI stakeholders. This position partners closely with Vehicle Engineering, Design, Service NPI, Manufacturing, Quality, Purchasing, Supply Chain, Technical Publications, Collision R&D, Service Operations, Insurance, and certified collision repair facilities in a fast-paced, highly collaborative environment. Responsibilities Lead collision repairability assessments for exterior systems and components beginning in concept, architecture, and advanced development phases and continuing through production launch. Evaluate repairability and replacement strategies for body sheet metal, including closures, fenders, quarter panels, body sides, bumper reinforcements, underbody exterior panels, and related structural or cosmetic assemblies. Translate collision repair requirements into clear design inputs, serviceability targets, and trade-off recommendations for Engineering and Design teams. Establish repair-versus-replace strategies that consider technician safety, repair quality, vehicle performance, customer experience, cycle time, parts availability and total repair cost. Apply RCAR standards and principles, along with recognized collision repair practices, to drive service-focused design concepts and improve vehicle insurability. Represent the voice of the technician and customer in design reviews, architecture decisions, development milestone reviews, prototype evaluations, and production readiness activities. Identify complex vehicle structure systems that may create repair challenges and develop simplified, repeatable, and clearly documented repair paths. Define permissible repair methods, limitations, sectioning or replacement boundaries, attachment strategies, joining requirements, corrosion protection, sealing, refinishing, and post-repair verification needs. Assess the impact of mixed materials, adhesives, rivets, welds, fasteners, composites, castings, high-strength steels, aluminum, and other joining or material technologies on collision repair. With the support of engineering define required tools, fixtures, equipment, and consumables for certified collision repair facilities. Participate in hands-on and virtual prototype, pilot, and validation repairs to confirm that proposed repair strategies can be executed safely, consistently, and efficiently in the field. Create and maintain service part numbers for collision-related components, subassemblies, kits, hardware, consumables, and repair-specific parts in the appropriate product lifecycle and service systems. Own the collision repair service bill of materials for new product introduction, ensuring accurate structure, applicability, service intent, supersession logic, interchangeability, and release status. Ensure service BOMs remain aligned with the latest production design, engineering changes, supplier changes, and approved repair strategies through disciplined change management. Define service assembly content and replacement packages where a repair is not technically, economically, or operationally appropriate at the individual component level. Partner with Technical Publications to convert engineering decisions into collision repair procedures, illustrations, labor-impact inputs, parts recommendations, training content, and technical communications. Develop repairability and insurability metrics, track progress through development, and escalate risks that could affect repair cost, repair cycle time, parts availability, facility capability, or customer satisfaction. Lead issue resolution for collision repair concerns using structured problem solving, root-cause analysis, and closed-loop corrective actions. Gather and analyze feedback from technicians, certified repair facilities, insurers, estimators, adjusters, and customers to identify opportunities for design, service content, parts, or process improvement. Coordinate field returns, repair observations, and part analysis to validate assumptions and improve future product designs. Support launch readiness, service introduction, repair network readiness, and field actions related to collision repairability and service parts. Build and maintain standards, playbooks, checklists, and design review tools that institutionalize prediction, prevention, and protection across vehicle programs. Drive change management activities by evaluating service impact, repair strategy, part interchangeability, documentation updates, and disposition of affected service content. Qualifications Bachelor’s degree in Automotive Technology, a related engineering/technical degree, or equivalent hands-on industry experience. Technical collision repair training, I-CAR training, OEM certification, ASE certification, or equivalent industry credentials are valued. Training or demonstrated proficiency in CAD, PLM, BOM management, technical documentation, or engineering change control is preferred. 8+ years of experience in collision repair, automotive service engineering, body repair, vehicle body structures, repair facility operations, estimating, insurance claims, or a closely related field. Demonstrated hands-on knowledge of collision repair processes for exterior body and trim components. Strong understanding of repair-versus-replace decision-making and the factors that influence vehicle insurability, repair cost, cycle time, safety, and customer experience. Experience interpreting engineering drawings, CAD data, service procedures, parts catalogs, or repair manuals. Experience working with part numbering, bills of material, engineering change management, or product lifecycle management systems. title: Senior Manager, Consulting Services
description:
Who we are
Samsara (NYSE: IOT) is the pioneer of the Connected Operations™ Cloud, which is a platform that enables organizations that depend on physical operations to harness Internet of Things (IoT) data to develop actionable insights and improve their operations. At Samsara, we are helping improve the safety, efficiency and sustainability of the physical operations that power our global economy. Representing more than 40% of global GDP, these industries are the infrastructure of our planet, including agriculture, construction, field services, transportation, and manufacturing — and we are excited to help digitally transform their operations at scale.
Working at Samsara means you’ll help define the future of physical operations and be on a team that’s shaping an exciting array of product solutions, including Video-Based Safety, Vehicle Telematics, Apps and Driver Workflows, and Equipment Monitoring. As part of a recently public company, you’ll have the autonomy and support to make an impact as we build for the long term.
About the role:
Samsara’s Consulting Services organization helps customers realize lasting value from our platform, from our largest enterprise accounts to thousands of customers in our Scale segment. Two teams do this work in different ways. Resident Consultants (RCs) are embedded long-term in enterprise customers, where they administer the platform, run adoption and change programs, and act as trusted advisors to customer executives. Training Specialists design and deliver one-to-many learning programs, including cohort-based sessions, live webinars, and digital assets, that help customers adopt the platform at scale.
As the Senior Manager, Consulting Services, you will lead the Resident Consultant team directly and the Training Specialist team through a frontline manager, and build the team needed to execute our strategy and roadmap for embedded and scaled services. You will play a key role in implementing strategic initiatives, improving operational efficiency, and raising the quality bar across both teams, while influencing the broader Customer Success function. This role requires a blend of strategic thinking, strong leadership, and a passion for customer outcomes. You will be a visible partner to Sales, Customer Success, Product, Finance, and Samsara executives.
This is a remote position open to candidates residing in the US. You will be able to travel within the United States for customer, team, and company needs (up to 25%).
You should apply if:
You want to impact the industries that run our world: The programs your teams deliver can affect whether truck drivers deliver goods on time and without accidents, whether students get dropped off safely from school, or whether power gets restored quickly after a natural disaster.
You thrive the most when solving problems: Our constantly expanding technology and the complexities faced by our customers provide an exciting range of challenges. With a growth mindset and a desire to learn, you will strategically partner with customers and internal teams to find unique solutions that keep operations safe, efficient, and sustainable.
You are a natural relationship builder: Whether the relationship is with customer executives or with cross-functional teams at Samsara, you are in constant communication and collaboration with key stakeholders to win as a team.
You are the architect of your own career: If you put in the work, this role won’t be your last at Samsara. This Customer Success organization is still shaping its future, and you will have plenty of autonomy and opportunities to master your craft in a hyper-growth environment.
You want to be with the best: At Samsara, we win together, celebrate together, and support each other. You will be surrounded by the best and brightest professionals out there.
In this role, you will:
Lead the Resident Consultant team directly and the Training Specialist team through a frontline manager, build the team needed to execute the strategy and roadmap, and make sure the two teams work together across the customer lifecycle.
Play a key role in implementing strategic initiatives for both service offerings, including packaging, pricing guardrails, and capacity planning, and in improving operational efficiency.
Ensure ongoing success and value realization for enterprise customers who use Resident Consultant services, and for the many customers who learn through our training programs.
Proactively identify opportunities to improve customer satisfaction, and develop and refine mechanisms to monitor customer experience, such as CSAT, value tracking, and learning outcomes.
Identify, assess, and mitigate operational and strategic risks across both teams, and develop risk management strategies, such as coverage plans, bench capacity, and escalation paths.
Set high standards for execution and champion operational excellence across both teams, including clear definitions of what "good" looks like for executive stakeholder communication, program delivery, and instructional quality.
Partner with Sales, Deal Desk, and Finance to scope, price, and staff new engagements, and to forecast headcount against demand.
Promote cross-team collaboration with Customer Success and Product to identify knowledge gaps and adoption barriers, and streamline the processes and workflows that connect these teams.
Keep executives informed of progress, report on team and customer outcomes, and advocate for change when needed.
Minimum requirements for the role:
6+ years managing teams in Customer Success, consulting, professional services, or customer education, including recruiting, developing, and retaining top talent.
Experience building or overseeing customer training or education programs delivered one-to-many, such as live virtual sessions, cohort-based programs, or digital learning.
Working knowledge of instructional design, and the ability to use engagement, adoption, and customer satisfaction data to improve programs and decisions.
Experience scaling a service offering, planning capacity, and partnering with Sales and Finance on scoping and pricing.
Exceptional executive stakeholder management and communication skills, emotional intelligence, and prioritization.
Proven track record of building trust and collaborating across teams, from customer executives to day-to-day users of our solutions and internal partners in Sales, Product, Engineering, and Finance.
Self-starter who takes initiative and thrives in a fast-paced, change-heavy environment.
Demonstrated ability to foster an inclusive team environment that values diverse perspectives.
Ability to travel within the United States for customer meetings, team events, and company events (up to 25%).
Bachelor’s degree from a 4-year institution.
An ideal candidate also has:
Led a team of customer-facing consultants delivering long-term engagements with Fortune 500 clients.
Coached or managed a frontline manager, led more than one team with distinct functions, or built a team from the ground up as demand grew.
Background in SaaS product training or customer education, and familiarity with LMS, Community, and virtual classroom platforms.

Beyond compensation, we provide the foundations that enable long-term success: a flexible, employee-led remote model, a professional development stipend, comprehensive health and parental leave plans, and more. Our goal is to ensure that all members of our team can contribute effectively, whether they are working on-site, in a hybrid model, or fully remotely. Belonging at Samsara

We depend on the unique approaches of our team members to help us solve complex problems and want to ensure that Samsara is a place where people from all backgrounds can make an impact.

title: engineer I, Operations Data Engineering (Seattle, WA)
location: 1101 Church ST, Nashville, Tennessee, United States
description:
Now Brewing – engineer I, Operations Data Engineering - ST! #tobeapartner
From the beginning, Starbucks set out to be a different kind of company. One that not only celebrated coffee and the rich tradition, but that also brought a feeling of connection. We are known for developing extraordinary leaders who share this passion and are guided by their service to others.
The Operations team within Data & AI Technology keeps Starbucks data platforms, pipelines, and applications healthy, available and trusted. We monitor production systems, respond to incidents, resolve data issues and continuously improve how our services run, so that partners, analysts and business teams can rely on accurate, on-time data every day.
As an Engineer I, you will be part Operations Engineering team part of Data & AI Technology, you will be part of the front line that keeps system up and running. You will resolve support tickets, triage alerts troubleshoot failures and restore service, working closely with senior engineers, development teams, and delivery partners. Over time you will help core engineering team helps in automation and strengthen monitoring so that issues are caught earlier. This role suits an early-career engineer who enjoys problem-solving, stays calm under pressure and takes pride in reliability.
What you will do
Monitor applications and platform health using dashboards, alerts and logs, and act quickly on failures or delays.
Triage, investigate and resolve incidents and service requests within agreed service levels, escalating to senior engineers or owning teams when needed.
Investigate data quality and data latency issues, identify root causes and coordinate fixes with upstream and downstream teams.
Create and maintain runbooks, standard operating procedures, and knowledge articles.
Support production deployments, change requests and release validation in line with change management processes.
Automate repetitive operational tasks and improve alerting and monitoring coverage.
We'd love to hear from people with:
Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Engineering or related field.
1–2+ years of experience in production support, IT operations, data engineering or software development (internships and co-ops count).
Solid knowledge of SQL for querying and validating data.
Working knowledge of a scripting language such as Python, PySpark, and PowerShell.
Strong troubleshooting skills and attention to detail.
Clear written and verbal communication, especially when updating stakeholders during an incident.
Preferred qualifications:
Experience in Microsoft Azure or AWS and Databricks
Experience with job scheduling and orchestration tools, and with monitoring tools such as , Airflow, Azure Data Factory, Azure Monitor or Log Analytics.
Familiarity with IT service management tools such as ServiceNow and with ITIL practices.
Strong understanding of ETL/ELT pipelines and data warehousing concepts.
Exposure to CI/CD, Git and release processes.

Crafting the world’s finest coffee, one meaningful moment at a time
We believe in creating a warm and welcoming space where every cup of coffee sparks connection.   As a coffeehouse leader, you don’t just run a business—you lead a team that creates moments of connection and joy.    Every day provides an opportunity to lead with craft and heart, making your coffeehouse a place where your community feels welcome.
We are invested in your growth journey, empowered through developmental experiences as well as our industry leading benefits .
We'd love to hear from people with:
3 years retail / customer service management experience or 4+ years of US Military service
Strong organizational, interpersonal and problem solving skills
Entrepreneurial mentality with experience in a sales focused environment
Strong leadership skills and the ability to coach and mentor team partners with professional maturity
Minimum High School or GED
Requirements:
Legal documentation establishing your identity and eligibility to be legally employed in the country in which you apply.
Ability to work full time (the work regularly demands in excess of 40 hours per week) including variable hours including early mornings, evenings, weekends and/ or holidays.
Let us give you the opportunity to grow as an individual, to build lasting relationships and make an impact in a place where people, quality and value mean everything.
Join us and connect with something bigger, apply today!
As a Starbucks partner, you (and your family) will have access to medical, dental, vision, basic and supplemental life insurance, and other voluntary insurance benefits. Partners have access to short-term and long-term disability, paid parental leave, family expansion reimbursement, paid vacation from date of hire*, sick time (accrued at 1 hour for every 25 hours worked), eight paid holidays, and two personal days per year. Starbucks also offers eligible partners participation in a 401(k) retirement plan with employer match, a discounted company stock program (S.I.P.), Starbucks equity program (Bean Stock), incentivized emergency savings, and financial well-being tools.  Additionally, Starbucks offers 100% upfront tuition coverage for a first-time bachelor’s degree through Arizona State University’s online program via the Starbucks College Achievement Plan, student loan management resources, and access to other educational opportunities.  You will also have access to backup care and DACA reimbursement.   Starbucks will comply with any applicable state and local laws regarding employee leave benefits, including, but not limited to providing time off pursuant to the Colorado Healthy Families and Workplaces Act, and in accordance with its plans and policies. This list is subject to change depending on collective bargaining in locations where partners have a certified bargaining representative. For additional information regarding partner perks and more detailed information about benefits, go to starbucksbenefits.com .
*If you are working in CA, CO, IL, LA, ME, MA, NE, ND or RI, you will accrue vacation up to a maximum of 120 hours (190 in CA) for roles below director and 200 hours (316 in CA) for roles at director or above.  For roles in other states, you will be granted vacation time starting at 120 hours annually for roles below director and 200 hours annually for roles director and above.
The actual base pay offered to the successful candidate will be based on multiple factors, including but not limited to job-related knowledge/skills, experience, geographical location, and internal equity.  At Starbucks, it is not typical for an individual to be hired at the high end of the range for their role, and compensation decisions are dependent upon the facts and circumstances of each position and candidate.
Starbucks Coffee Company is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, national origin, disability, or protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law. Qualified applicants with criminal histories will be considered for employment in a manner consistent with all federal, state and local ordinances.
Starbucks Coffee Company is committed to offering reasonable accommodations to job applicants with disabilities. If you need assistance or an accommodation due to a disability, please contact us at applicantaccommodation@starbucks.com or 1(888) 611-2258.

title: AI Transformation Lead, Marketing
location: San Francisco, New York, Seattle, Chicago, Atlanta, Remote in the US
description:
Who we are
About Stripe
Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies — from the world's largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups — use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone's reach while doing the most important work of your career.
About the team
The Stripe Marketing organization is undergoing a fundamental transformation in how it works. We're building a team of Forward Deployed AI Accelerators (FDAs) embedded directly with marketing cohorts to make AI the default mode for all work — not an occasional tool, but the foundation of how every marketer at Stripe executes.
Today, marketers are already achieving remarkable results — building their own data dashboards, creating agents that compress multi-day processes, and authoring tools that accelerate workflows. The FDA team exists to take what's working and systematically scale it across the entire marketing organization.
What you'll do
As a Forward Deployed AI Accelerator, you'll be embedded with a cohort of 25–45 marketers organized by functional team, shared workflow, or location. You'll build alongside them, and you'll help them fundamentally change how they operate. Your measure of success is the number of workflows you've permanently transformed and the extent to which those in your cohort start any task with an AI tool.
Responsibilities
Identify and document the highest-leverage workflow transformations within your cohort's day-to-day work by deeply understanding their processes and outputs
Build custom tools, agents, automations, and skills tailored to each marketer's specific responsibilities
Coach and partner with each marketer through a progressive journey — from awareness, to first win, to regular AI integration, to full workflow transformation, to self-sufficiency
Teach marketers to build and iterate on their own tools over time, creating independence
Recognize patterns across your cohort and systematically scale what works — a tool built for one marketer will be reusable for their peers
Document every tool, playbook, and transformation pattern you build so the entire FDA team uses each other's work
Share wins visibly within your cohort and with leadership to build momentum, inspire, and celebrate success
Track individual and cohort progress rigorously against a defined maturity model, moving every marketer toward self-sustaining, AI-first work
Prepare marketers for an agentic future — not just prompt writing, but designing, building, and overseeing autonomous, multi-agent workflows
Who you are
We're looking for people who have already lived the transformation they'll be driving for others. You've used AI to fundamentally change how work gets done, not as a novelty, but as your default operating mode.
You are a deep AI practitioner. You build agents, automations, and tools fluently. You don't just know what AI can do in theory. You've built things that changed how real teams operate, and the people you built for actually use what you shipped. You build in real time alongside the people you support.
You spot transformation opportunities and execute on them. You look at a team's workflows and see where AI changes the economics: where existing work can be done in a fraction of the time, or where entirely new programs become viable that weren't worth doing before. Then you build the thing, not just the slide.
You understand marketing work. You either have direct experience in marketing or quickly learn the workflows, deliverables, tools, and pressures of your assigned cohort. You know that understanding someone's work is a prerequisite to transforming it.
You are a pattern recognizer. When you build something that works for one person, you immediately see how it applies to others. You think in systems, not one-off solutions.
You are a strong communicator. You explain technical concepts clearly to non-technical audiences, adapt your style to different people, and make progress visible to leadership and stakeholders.
You are high-caliber, persistent, and versatile. Your skills and experience are valuable across the company. You're the kind of person who succeeds in many roles at Stripe.
You bias toward action and speed. You'd rather show someone a working proof-of-concept on their own deliverable today than present a polished deck about what's theoretically possible next quarter.
You are comfortable with ambiguity and evolution. This is a new team building a new operating model. The playbook will be rewritten as we learn. You thrive in that environment.
Minimum requirements
5+ years of professional experience in a role requiring diagnostic thinking, problem-solving, and cross-functional collaboration
Demonstrated, hands-on experience building and deploying AI-powered agents, tools, automations, or workflows that real people use in their actual work, whether that made existing processes meaningfully more efficient or made previously unviable work possible for the first time
Proficiency with AI development tools and platforms (e.g., Claude Code, Codex, custom agent frameworks, API integrations, workflow automation tools)
Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain technical concepts to non-technical audiences and adapt your style to different learners
Comfort working across multiple workstreams and relationships simultaneously (you'll be supporting 25–45 marketers at varying stages of their AI journey)
Track record of coaching, teaching, or enabling others, with evidence that people you've helped actually changed how they work
Preferred qualifications
Experience in a formal AI transformation role where the job was substantially about identifying opportunities for workflow transformation and executing on them with hands-on builds
Experience helping people become more expert AI users and capable builders
Experience in marketing, marketing operations, growth, or a closely adjacent function, including familiarity with marketing technology stacks (e.g., Marketo, Salesforce, analytics platforms, content management tools)

Build qualified and inclusive pipelines through hands-on sourcing across communities, referrals, events, market mapping, relationship-based outreach, and other creative channels beyond inbound applications and standard LinkedIn outreach
Partner consultatively with hiring managers to translate business priorities into clear role requirements, search strategies, structured assessments, and timely decisions
Use funnel metrics, market evidence, and candidate feedback to identify risks, recommend actions, and communicate progress without allowing reporting or process to substitute for recruiting
Deliver a thoughtful candidate experience and maintain relationships with prospective candidates for immediate and future needs
Serve as an operational bridge between OpenRouter and Stripe by absorbing coordination where possible, maintaining continuity, and reducing the time OpenRouter leaders spend navigating recruiting processes

Experience partnering consultatively with hiring managers, managing multiple searches, and using recruiting metrics and market evidence to identify risk and guide action

Experience supporting structured, competency-based hiring processes

title: Senior Treasury Specialist, Bridge Capital & Liquidity Risk – Digital Assets
description:
About Stripe and Bridge
Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world's largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone's reach while doing the most important work of your career.
Bridge is a subsidiary of Stripe that is building a new payments platform powered by stablecoins to make global money movement simpler, faster, and more accessible. Through our APIs, businesses can send and receive funds across borders, give customers access to dollars through virtual accounts, and disburse USD globally.
About the team
We are seeking a Senior Treasury Specialist to oversee capital adequacy, liquidity stress testing, financial risk management, and contingency funding planning for Bridge National Trust Bank (BNTB)'s Treasury and Reserve Operations. Issuing digital assets that are fully backed by reserves raises new questions for a regulated bank: how much capital and liquidity it needs, how it holds up under stress, and how it shows management, the Board, and regulators that it is safe and sound.
What you'll do
In this role, you will support Stripe’s proposed national trust bank, Bridge National Trust Bank (BNTB), currently in formation and subject to full regulatory approval by the OCC. You will build and run the bank's capital, liquidity, and financial risk management framework and the governance around it. That includes the analysis, monitoring, policies, and reporting that let the bank grow safely as regulatory requirements for stablecoin issuers continue to evolve.
You will partner closely with the BNTB Treasury and Reserve Operations team, the broader Bridge and Stripe treasury team, risk, compliance, finance, accounting, regulatory reporting, product, data science, and engineering. In the near term, you will help design the frameworks and put the first cycles into practice. As the bank scales, you will turn them into repeatable, automated processes.
Responsibilities
Own capital planning and the ongoing assessment of the bank's capital adequacy
Own and report on capital, liquidity, and financial risk metrics against risk appetite and limits; escalate breaches and emerging trends
Design and run liquidity and capital stress testing, and turn the results into recommendations for funding and capital strategy
Own contingency funding planning, including annual testing and tracking remediation to closure
Maintain treasury risk policies and procedures, and prepare management and Board reporting
Provide risk oversight of reserve and investment activity (counterparty, concentration, liquidity and interest rate risk); partner with product, data science, and engineering to automate monitoring and reporting
Coordinate with the broader Stripe treasury team on capital management initiatives including consolidated capital planning, infrastructure and methodology development and governance frameworks
Who you are
You are a builder - we are building a new OCC  chartered bank and we are looking for folks who thrive in a fast-paced, growing environment. This means one day you may be working on a stress testing methodology and the next day speaking with engineers about a critical liquidity concept to be incorporated into systems. You will thrive here if that energizes you, if you take ownership of whatever is needed, and if you bring the same rigor to a stress test assumption as you do to a Board memo. You combine the discipline of a risk manager with the instincts of a builder, and you can explain capital and liquidity concepts clearly to treasury, product, and engineering partners.
We're looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.
Minimum requirements
7-10 years of experience in treasury, capital planning, liquidity risk, stress testing, or financial risk management
Hands-on experience building or running capital or liquidity frameworks at a regulated US financial institution
Experience writing and presenting on policies, procedures, or management and Board materials
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, including the ability to assess incomplete information and make sound recommendations
Strong experience using AI tools to build, automate, and improve workflows and data analytics
Strong communication skills and the ability to build relationships across treasury, risk, finance, product, and engineering
Based in or willing to relocate to New York
Preferred qualifications
Experience at a bank regulated by the OCC or Federal Reserve
Interest rate or fixed-income risk analytics
Experience with SQL, Python, or equivalent for analysis and reporting
Interest in digital assets or stablecoins

Optimize end-to-end latency, reasoning chains, and output interpretability for clinical and scientific research end-users.
